nodes.meaning: write phase, field transmission, absorbed loss fraction, and optional delay for one ring/data level.
comments: write phase, field transmission, absorbed loss fraction, and optional delay for one ring/data level.
lam_l contains L laser wavelengths in m.
shift is the resonance shift in m.
fca_loss is the ring-level junction loss in 1/m.
loss_tfac is the dimensionless temperature multiplier.
write row k of phase in rad, amplitude transmission, absorbed fraction, and optional round-trip delay in s.
x = lambda_line - shift and d = x - lambda_res locate the laser on the cold phase curve.
n(x) = n_eff + (n_eff - n_g)*d/lambda_res - (dn_g/dlambda)*d^2/(2*lambda_res).
phase = 2*pi*n(x)*L/x.
this second-order expansion uses dn_eff/dlambda = (n_eff - n_g)/lambda.
its phase equals 2*pi*m when the shifted resonance reaches the laser, for any shift.
round-trip delay is (n_g + (dn_g/dlambda)*d)*L/C0.
phase sensitivity to shift is 2*pi*n_g(x)*L/x^2.
the measured cold resonance already contains the coupler phase.
downstream optics uses psi=0 to avoid counting the coupler phase twice.
alpha = (alpha_ref + fca_loss - fca_ref)*loss_tfac.
keep non-absorbing loss fixed, so absorbing loss is alpha - alpha_nonheat.
field transmission is exp(-alpha*L/2), and absorbed fraction is alpha_heat/alpha.
clamp loss and absorbed fraction to their physical bounds.
temperature scales the full intrinsic loss - the added loss is treated as absorptive.
every resonance order shifts by the same amount, preserving cold wavelength FSR.
the extracted rib160 mode table has thermal dispersion kappa_to=4.1–4.5e-4 per nm.
this is not an optical decay rate.
the missing correction is approximately kappa_to*shift*abs(order_wavelength - lambda_res).
it is 0.43 percent of shift per FSR — about 33 pm at adjacent orders and 66 pm at second orders for the 7.6 nm g26 lock shift.
at 13 nm shift, adjacent-order error is about 57 pm.
the locked order is exact.
this affects foreign-line heating and monitor background — about -0.15 to +0.14 percent of g26 absorbed power and up to about 1 percent in FSR stress corners.
BND-1 checks the other-order spacing in linewidths.
model versus solver spacings are 2.79 versus about 2.88 for g26, 1.68 versus about 1.82 for window A, and 1.33 versus about 1.26 for fsr_edge.
their classes agree.
test_rigid_comb_against_the_solver_table in tests/verification/test_phase.py checks this limitation.
the full n_eff(lambda, T, V)*L(T) law needs a thermal-dispersion config key and coordinated changes to the engine, oracle, replicas, and calibration.

@njit(cache=True, _nrt=False)
def write_ring_optical_inputs_for_data_level(
    ring_parameters: Float64Matrix,  # ring_parameters = R_ring (mixed units) - packed RP_* parameters, one row per ring - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, RING_PARAMETER_COLUMN_COUNT)
    ring_index: int,  # ring_index = k (1) - physical ring index - type int scalar
    laser_wavelengths_m: Float64Vector,  # laser_wavelengths_m = lambda_L (m) - vacuum laser wavelengths - type float64 ndarray, shape (L,)
    resonance_shift_m: float,  # resonance_shift_m = Delta_lambda_r (m) - thermal and junction resonance shift - type float scalar
    junction_power_loss_per_m: float,  # junction_power_loss_per_m = f*alpha_FCA (1/m) - ring-level junction power-loss coefficient - type float scalar
    loss_temperature_factor: float,  # loss_temperature_factor = s_alpha (1) - temperature multiplier for intrinsic loss - type float scalar
    out_round_trip_phase_rad: Float64Matrix,  # out_round_trip_phase_rad = phi (rad) - round-trip phases written in row k - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_round_trip_field_transmission: Float64Matrix,  # out_round_trip_field_transmission = a (1) - retained round-trip field amplitudes written in row k - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_absorbed_loss_fraction: Float64Matrix,  # out_absorbed_loss_fraction = eta (1) - absorbed shares of intrinsic loss written in row k - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_round_trip_delay_s: Float64Matrix,  # out_round_trip_delay_s = T_rt (s) - round-trip group delays written at data level zero - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    write_round_trip_delay: bool,  # write_round_trip_delay = delay_enabled (1) - also write round-trip group delay - type bool scalar
) -> (
    None  # return = None - results are written into the output buffers - type None
):
    cold_resonance_m = ring_parameters[ring_index, RING_PARAMETER_COLUMN_COLD_RESONANCE_WAVELENGTH]
    reference_effective_index = ring_parameters[ring_index, RING_PARAMETER_COLUMN_EFFECTIVE_INDEX]
    reference_group_index = ring_parameters[ring_index, RING_PARAMETER_COLUMN_GROUP_INDEX]
    d_group_index_d_wavelength_per_m = ring_parameters[ring_index, RING_PARAMETER_COLUMN_GROUP_INDEX_WAVELENGTH_DERIVATIVE]
    ring_length_m = ring_parameters[ring_index, RING_PARAMETER_COLUMN_ROUND_TRIP_LENGTH]
    intrinsic_power_loss_per_m = (
        ring_parameters[ring_index, RING_PARAMETER_COLUMN_INTRINSIC_POWER_LOSS_PER_LENGTH] + junction_power_loss_per_m - ring_parameters[ring_index, RING_PARAMETER_COLUMN_REFERENCE_JUNCTION_POWER_LOSS_PER_LENGTH]
    )  # intrinsic loss before temperature scaling, 1/m
    intrinsic_power_loss_per_m *= loss_temperature_factor  # intrinsic loss after temperature scaling, 1/m
    if intrinsic_power_loss_per_m < 0.0:
        intrinsic_power_loss_per_m = 0.0
    round_trip_field_transmission = math.exp(-0.5 * intrinsic_power_loss_per_m * ring_length_m)
    absorptive_power_loss_per_m = intrinsic_power_loss_per_m - ring_parameters[ring_index, RING_PARAMETER_COLUMN_NONABSORPTIVE_POWER_LOSS_PER_LENGTH]  # alpha_heat [1/m]
    if absorptive_power_loss_per_m < 0.0:
        absorptive_power_loss_per_m = 0.0
    absorbed_share_of_intrinsic_loss = (
        absorptive_power_loss_per_m / intrinsic_power_loss_per_m if intrinsic_power_loss_per_m > 0.0 else 0.0
    )
    if absorbed_share_of_intrinsic_loss > 1.0:
        absorbed_share_of_intrinsic_loss = 1.0
    for line_index in range(laser_wavelengths_m.shape[0]):
        cold_wavelength_m = laser_wavelengths_m[line_index] - resonance_shift_m  # laser wavelength on the cold phase curve
        wavelength_offset_m = cold_wavelength_m - cold_resonance_m
        effective_index_at_cold_wavelength = (
            reference_effective_index
            + (reference_effective_index - reference_group_index) * wavelength_offset_m / cold_resonance_m
            - 0.5
            * d_group_index_d_wavelength_per_m
            * wavelength_offset_m
            * wavelength_offset_m
            / cold_resonance_m
        )
        out_round_trip_phase_rad[ring_index, line_index] = (
            _TWO_PI * effective_index_at_cold_wavelength * ring_length_m / cold_wavelength_m
        )
        out_round_trip_field_transmission[ring_index, line_index] = round_trip_field_transmission
        out_absorbed_loss_fraction[ring_index, line_index] = absorbed_share_of_intrinsic_loss
        if write_round_trip_delay:
            # group delay in s
            out_round_trip_delay_s[ring_index, line_index] = (
                (reference_group_index + d_group_index_d_wavelength_per_m * wavelength_offset_m)
                * ring_length_m
                / C0
            )

    level_zero_reverse_bias_v: Float64Vector,  # level_zero_reverse_bias_v = V_0 (V) - reverse bias at data level zero - type float64 ndarray, shape (N,)
    level_one_reverse_bias_v: Float64Vector,  # level_one_reverse_bias_v = V_1 (V) - reverse bias at data level one - type float64 ndarray, shape (N,)
    bias_grid_v: Float64Vector,  # bias_grid_v = V_grid (V) - junction reverse-bias grid - type float64 ndarray, shape (G,)
    junction_index_change_table: Float64Vector,  # junction_index_change_table = Delta_n_eff (1) - junction effective-index changes on the bias grid - type float64 ndarray, shape (G,)
    junction_loss_table_per_m: Float64Vector,  # junction_loss_table_per_m = alpha_FCA (1/m) - junction power-loss coefficients on the bias grid - type float64 ndarray, shape (G,)
    junction_capacitance_table_f_per_m: Float64Vector,  # junction_capacitance_table_f_per_m = c_j (F/m) - junction capacitance per length on the bias grid - type float64 ndarray, shape (G,)
    junction_resistance_table_ohm_m: Float64Vector,  # junction_resistance_table_ohm_m = r_s (ohm*m) - junction resistance-length products on the bias grid - type float64 ndarray, shape (G,)
    out_level_zero_phase_rad: Float64Matrix,  # out_level_zero_phase_rad = phi_0 (rad) - level-0 round-trip phases written in place - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_level_one_phase_rad: Float64Matrix,  # out_level_one_phase_rad = phi_1 (rad) - level-1 round-trip phases written in place - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_level_zero_field_transmission: Float64Matrix,  # out_level_zero_field_transmission = a_0 (1) - level-0 retained round-trip field amplitudes written in place - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_level_one_field_transmission: Float64Matrix,  # out_level_one_field_transmission = a_1 (1) - level-1 retained round-trip field amplitudes written in place - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_level_zero_absorbed_loss_fraction: Float64Matrix,  # out_level_zero_absorbed_loss_fraction = eta_0 (1) - level-0 absorbed shares of intrinsic loss written in place - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_level_one_absorbed_loss_fraction: Float64Matrix,  # out_level_one_absorbed_loss_fraction = eta_1 (1) - level-1 absorbed shares of intrinsic loss written in place - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_through_power_coupling: Float64Matrix,  # out_through_power_coupling = K_th^2 (1) - per-pass coupler power fractions written in place - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_drop_power_coupling: Float64Matrix,  # out_drop_power_coupling = K_dr^2 (1) - per-pass coupler power fractions written in place - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_round_trip_delay_s: Float64Matrix,  # out_round_trip_delay_s = T_rt (s) - round-trip group delays written at data level zero - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, L)
    out_resonance_shift_m: Float64Matrix,  # out_resonance_shift_m = Delta_lambda_r (m) - resonance shifts written for both binary data levels - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, 2)
    out_junction_capacitance_f: Float64Matrix,  # out_junction_capacitance_f = C_j (F) - ring junction capacitance written for both binary data levels - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, 2)
    out_series_resistance_ohm: Float64Matrix,  # out_series_resistance_ohm = R_s (ohm) - ring series resistance written for both binary data levels - type float64 ndarray, shape (N, 2)
    out_junction_flags: Int8Vector,  # out_junction_flags = flags (1) - junction clipping flags updated in place - type int8 ndarray, shape (N,)
) -> (
    None  # return = None - results are written into the output buffers - type None
):
    evaluate_binary_ring_optical_inputs(ring_parameters, laser_wavelengths_m, t_ring_k, t_heater_k, level_zero_reverse_bias_v, level_one_reverse_bias_v, bias_grid_v, junction_index_change_table, junction_loss_table_per_m, junction_capacitance_table_f_per_m, junction_resistance_table_ohm_m, out_level_zero_phase_rad,
                           out_level_one_phase_rad, out_level_zero_field_transmission, out_level_one_field_transmission, out_level_zero_absorbed_loss_fraction, out_level_one_absorbed_loss_fraction, out_round_trip_delay_s, out_resonance_shift_m, out_junction_capacitance_f, out_series_resistance_ohm,
                           out_junction_flags)
    evaluate_coupler_power_fractions(ring_parameters, laser_wavelengths_m, out_through_power_coupling, out_drop_power_coupling)

source_ref.code:
def __init__(self, pp, scenario: Scenario | None = None, spec: ControllerSpec | None = None, *, cfg=None,
                 controller_latency_ticks: int = 0, noise_seed: int = 0, scenario_seed: int = 0,
                 metrics: MetricsSpec | None = None, record=None, record_ticks: int = 0,
                 substep_policy: str | None = None, auto_max_ticks: int = 64, fast_kernel: bool = False,
                 oracle: bool = True, histogram: bool | None = None, calibrate_aggressors: bool = True,
                 sh_tol_k: float = DEFAULT_SH_TOL_K):
        self.pp = pp
        self.sh_tol_k = float(sh_tol_k)
        B, N, L = int(pp.batch), int(pp.n_rings), int(pp.n_lines)
        self.B, self.N, self.L = B, N, L
        self.dt = float(pp.timing.dt_s)
        sysm = pp.thermal.system
        if sysm is None:
            raise ValueError("PlantParams has no thermal system (realize with thermal_hook='auto')")
        self.sys = sysm
        sc = Scenario(name="static") if scenario is None else scenario
        self.aggressor_calibration = {}
        if sc.pending_aggressors and calibrate_aggressors:
            sc, self.aggressor_calibration = prepare_scenario(sc, pp)
        self.scenario = sc
        if spec is None:
            if cfg is None:
                raise ValueError("Plant needs a ControllerSpec (or cfg to build one)")
            spec = ControllerSpec.from_config(cfg, n_batch=B, nominal=cfg, scenario_drives=sc.drives,
                                              scenario_offsets=sc.offsets)
        if spec.n_batch != B or spec.n_rings != N or spec.n_lines != L:
            raise ValueError(f"spec is for (B, N, L) = {(spec.n_batch, spec.n_rings, spec.n_lines)}, the plant has "
                             f"{(B, N, L)}")
        if abs(spec.tick_s - self.dt) > 1e-15 * self.dt:
            raise ValueError("spec.tick_s differs from pp.timing.dt_s")
        self.spec = spec
        self.maps = ChannelMaps.from_spec(spec)
        self.validator = ActionValidator(spec)
        self.controller_latency_ticks = int(controller_latency_ticks)
        self.noise_seed = int(noise_seed)
        self.scenario_seed = int(scenario_seed)
        pol = substep_policy if substep_policy is not None else ("fixed", "auto")[int(pp.timing.substep_policy)]
        if pol not in ("fixed", "auto"):
            raise ValueError("substep_policy must be 'fixed' or 'auto'")
        self.substep_policy = pol
        self.metrics_spec = MetricsSpec() if metrics is None else metrics
        self._record_specs = record
        self._record_ticks = int(record_ticks)
        self._fast_on = bool(fast_kernel)
        self._oracle_on = bool(oracle) and self.metrics_spec.oracle
        if self.metrics_spec.lock_reference == "oracle" and not self._oracle_on:
            raise ValueError("metrics lock_reference='oracle' needs the oracle (Plant(oracle=True))")
        self._histogram = histogram
        amp = int(max(0, math.floor(math.log2(max(int(auto_max_ticks), 1))))) if pol == "auto" else 0
        self._au_max_pow = amp
        self._build(amp)
        self._ctrl = None
        self.n_threads = None
        self.tick = 0
        self.reset()

nodes.name: _build
nodes.meaning: build
comments: build
pack module parameters, allocate state, and size queues for the declared timing.
KParams holds constants.
KState holds mutable arrays and scratch space.
keep these field names aligned with mrm.sim.state_spec.
each array must be writeable and C-contiguous to reuse the compiled engine.

source_ref.code:
def _build(self, au_max_pow: int) -> None:
        pp, spec, sysm = self.pp, self.spec, self.sys
        B, N, L = self.B, self.N, self.L
        dt = self.dt
        nseeds = rng.batch_seeds(self.noise_seed, B)
        sseeds = rng.batch_seeds(self.scenario_seed, B)
        self._nseeds, self._sseeds = nseeds, sseeds
        # phase / junction
        phase_prm = phase.PhaseParams.from_plant_params(pp)
        self.phase = phase_prm
        # self-heating rows (mrm.plant.optics.pack_self_heating_optical_state), one per world.
        # the bus segment transmissions are constants of the world (mrm.plant.phase equation 6), every other row entry is rewritten by the kernel
        if int(pp.flags.optics_model):
            raise ValueError("TCMT is archived - use exact ring optics")
        method = "exact"
        lam0 = C0 / np.asarray(pp.laser.line_freq_hz, float)
        bus_t2 = phase.calculate_bus_segment_power_transmission(pp)
        rows = []
        for b in range(B):
            rows.append(
                optics.pack_self_heating_optical_state(
                    np.zeros(L),
                    np.zeros((N, L)),
                    np.full((N, L), 1e-3),
                    np.full((N, L), 1e-4),
                    np.full((N, L), 0.99),
                    np.full((N, L), 1e-13),
                    np.full((N, L), 0.5),
                    lam0[b],
                    np.full(N, 300.0),
                    np.full(N, 7e-11),
                    0.0,
                    bus_order=np.asarray(pp.layout.bus_order),
                    bus_t2=bus_t2[b],
                    bus_t2_out=1.0,
                    rb=np.asarray(pp.optics.backscatter_rb[b]),
                    nrz={
                        "p1": np.full(N, 0.5),
                        "phi1": np.zeros((N, L)),
                        "a1": np.full((N, L), 0.99),
                        "eta1": np.full((N, L), 0.5),
                    },
                    method=method,
                    m_orders=int(pp.optics.tcmt_orders),
                )
            )
        packed_f0, packed_i = kernel.extend_selfheat_rows(
            np.stack([r[0] for r in rows]), np.stack([r[1] for r in rows])
        )
        self._packed_f0 = packed_f0
        # actuator paths
        heater_prm = electrical.HeaterDriverParams.from_plant_params(pp)
        bias_prm = electrical.BiasDacParams.from_plant_params(pp)
        self.heater_params, self.bias_params = heater_prm, bias_prm
        # sensors
        mon_hw = sensing.MonitorHw.from_plant_params(pp)
        self.monitor_hw = mon_hw
        temp_hw = sensing.TempSensorsHw.from_plant_params(pp)
        self.temp_hw = temp_hw
        rb_on = bool(getattr(pp.heater, "readback_present", False))
        rb_hw = sensing.ReadbackHw.from_plant_params(pp) if rb_on else None
        self.readback_hw = rb_hw
        dp_hw = DatapathHw.from_plant_params(pp)
        self.datapath_hw = dp_hw
        if dp_hw.mode == PATTERN_PRBS and dp_hw.prbs_k <= PRBS_TABLE_MAX_K:
            words, pre, prbs_period = prbs_table(dp_hw.prbs_k)
        else:
            words, pre, prbs_period = np.zeros(1, np.int64), np.zeros(2, np.int64), 0
        las_hw = LaserHw.from_plant_params(pp)
        self.laser_hw = las_hw
        # scenario
        sysm_agg = tuple(sysm.src_names[i] for i in sysm.aggressor_src)
        scen_arr = self.scenario.compile(
            dt_s=dt, n_rings=N, n_lines=L, batch=B, seed=self.scenario_seed, aggressor_sites=sysm_agg
        )
        self.scen_arrays = scen_arr
        # thermal coefficient tables — the exact first-order hold for a step of h = 2^p ticks, p = 0 ..
        # au_max_pow (the fixed policy uses p = 0 only. the auto policy steps by powers of two)
        tabs = [sysm.coefficients(dt * (1 << p)) for p in range(au_max_pow + 1)]
        th_a = np.ascontiguousarray(np.stack([t[0] for t in tabs], axis=1))
        th_c0 = np.ascontiguousarray(np.stack([t[1] for t in tabs], axis=1))
        th_c1 = np.ascontiguousarray(np.stack([t[2] for t in tabs], axis=1))
        # controller edges / periods
        period = int(spec.period_ticks)
        pop = period + int(spec.tick_jitter_ticks)

nodes.name: reset
nodes.meaning: reset
comments: reset
restore every world to its defined starting state at tick k0.
thermal history matters when the same inputs support a cold and a hot equilibrium.
'laser_ramp' increases laser power from zero over pp.timing.reset_ramp_ticks.
'branch_low' turns lasers on and starts the root search from the cold end.
'branch_high' starts from the hot end.
protocol defaults to pp.timing.reset_protocol.

nodes.name: settle
nodes.meaning: find a warm starting state from the held inputs immediately after reset.
comments: find a warm starting state from the held inputs immediately after reset.
run the same engine with each lag's infinite-step coefficients — a=0, c0=0, c1=residue.
each iteration includes implicit self-heating, heater TCR, bias, NRZ levels, and data-activity heat.
the first root search starts from the reset branch.
later searches continue from the previous root.
cross-ring optical heat and heater TCR use the previous iterate.
their small gains permit convergence.
this is the engine's fixed point, rather than a separate steady-state model.
hold both scenario endpoints at reset tick k0.
otherwise early events would affect the starting state before their scheduled time.
ticks still advance internally, so noise, PRBS positions, and optional laser drift change each iteration.
laser drift is zero by default.
stop each world independently after at least three iterations when every ring changes by less than tol_k.
freeze that world's result so batching does not change it.
g26 noise moves the fixed point by about 0.5 mK per tick.
the default 2 mK threshold is a settling criterion, not solver precision.
from branch_high, iteration-limited root solves can descend about 10 K per iteration.
nominal g26 settles in about 20 iterations.
these intermediate failed solves remain counted.
reset sensors, metrics, records, edges, registers, and noise again.
retain only thermal states, observer temperatures, source powers, and the solved ring/heater/PD temperatures and powers.
pass the same heater_code and bias_code used for reset.
iterations is the largest per-world count.
iterations_per_world and converged_per_world have shape (B,).
converged requires every world to pass.
max_delta_k is the largest final temperature change.
selfheat_not_converged_last counts failed ring solves in each world's last iteration.
max_step_k is the largest temperature change during any iteration.
sh_dt_max_k is the temperature range covered by the optical curvature bounds.
first iterations can exceed it — about 100 K from branch_low or 240 K from branch_high in nominal g26.
see DEFAULT_SH_DT_MAX_K.

source_ref.code:
def settle(self, *, heater_code=None, bias_code=None, max_iter: int = 200, tol_k: float = 2e-3) -> dict:
        if self.tick != self.k_reset:
            raise RuntimeError("settle() must follow reset() directly")
        P0 = self.P
        if int(P0.reset_protocol) == 0:
            raise ValueError("settle needs the reset protocol branch_low or branch_high (lasers on at the start); "
                             "laser_ramp starts dark")
        k0 = int(self.tick)
        B = self.B
        shape = P0.th_a.shape                                              # (B|1, n_pow, M)
        thermal_residues = np.asarray(self.sys.res_k_per_w, np.float64)
        c1 = np.ascontiguousarray(np.broadcast_to(thermal_residues[:, None, :], shape), dtype=np.float64).copy()
        held_signals = np.array(P0.sc_sig_i, dtype=np.int64, order="C", copy=True)
        held_signals[:, SI_NC] = 0                     # no signal is evaluated — S.sc_v0/sc_v1 retain the values at k0
        self.P = P0._replace(th_a=np.zeros(shape), th_c0=np.zeros(shape), th_c1=c1,
                             policy=type(P0.policy)(kernel.POLICY_FIXED), sc_sig_i=held_signals)
        S = self.S
        names = ("th_x", "th_t_obs", "th_g", "th_u0", "th_u1")
        rows = [kernel.RF_P_PREV, kernel.RF_T_RING, kernel.RF_T_HEATER, kernel.RF_T_PD, kernel.RF_T_NEW,
                kernel.RF_P_NEW, kernel.RF_HE_P, kernel.RF_P_ABS]     # the per-ring thermal rows that the settle keeps
        kept_thermal_state = {name: getattr(S, name).copy() for name in names}
        kept_ring_state = S.ring_float[:, rows, :].copy()

        # retain thermal state for the worlds selected by the (B,) mask.
        def freeze(worlds):
            for name in names:
                kept_thermal_state[name][worlds] = getattr(S, name)[worlds]
            kept_ring_state[worlds] = S.ring_float[worlds][:, rows, :]
        previous_temp_k = S.ring_float[:, kernel.RF_T_RING, :].copy()
        active_worlds = np.ones(B, bool)
        converged_worlds = np.zeros(B, bool)
        world_iterations = np.zeros(B, np.int64)
        world_delta_k = np.full(B, math.inf)
        world_max_step_k = np.zeros(B)
        world_failed_solves = np.zeros(B, np.int64)
        iteration = 0
        try:
            for iteration in range(1, int(max_iter) + 1):
                failures_before = S.world_int[:, kernel.WI_N_FAIL].copy()
                self.run(1, mode=kernel.MODE_OPEN)
                current_temp_k = S.ring_float[:, kernel.RF_T_RING, :]
                temp_change_k = np.max(np.abs(current_temp_k - previous_temp_k),
                    axis=1)                   # (B,) this iteration's change
                previous_temp_k = current_temp_k.copy()
                new_failed_solves = S.world_int[:, kernel.WI_N_FAIL] - failures_before
                world_iterations[active_worlds] = iteration
                world_delta_k[active_worlds] = temp_change_k[active_worlds]
                world_failed_solves[active_worlds] = new_failed_solves[active_worlds]
                world_max_step_k[active_worlds] = np.maximum(world_max_step_k[active_worlds],
                    temp_change_k[active_worlds])
                if iteration >= 3:
                    newly_converged = active_worlds & (temp_change_k < tol_k)
                    if np.any(newly_converged):
                        freeze(newly_converged)
                        converged_worlds |= newly_converged
                        active_worlds &= ~newly_converged
                if not np.any(active_worlds):
                    break
        finally:
            self.P = P0
        if np.any(active_worlds):
            freeze(active_worlds)  # max_iter reached — retain the last iterate without declaring convergence
        self._reset(None, k0=k0, protocol=None, heater_code=heater_code, bias_code=bias_code)
        S = self.S
        for name, val in kept_thermal_state.items():
            getattr(S, name)[...] = val
        S.ring_float[:, rows, :] = kept_ring_state
        S.ring_float[:, kernel.RF_T_BRANCH, :] = S.ring_float[:, kernel.RF_T_RING, :]
        self._init_t_adc()                                  # monitor_pd — the settled PD temperature
        return {"iterations": int(iteration), "iterations_per_world": world_iterations.copy(),
            "max_delta_k": float(np.max(world_delta_k)),
                "converged": bool(np.all(converged_worlds)), "converged_per_world": converged_worlds.copy(),
                "selfheat_not_converged_last": world_failed_solves.copy(),
                    "max_step_k": float(np.max(world_max_step_k)),
                "sh_dt_max_k": float(P0.dt_max_k)}

def _reset(self, noise_seed: int | None = None, *, k0: int = 0, protocol: str | None = None, heater_code=None,
               bias_code=None) -> None:
        if noise_seed is not None and int(noise_seed) != self.noise_seed:
            self.noise_seed = int(noise_seed)
            self._rekey_noise()
        P, S = self.P, self.S
        B, N, L = self.B, self.N, self.L
        if protocol is not None:
            codes = {"laser_ramp": 0, "branch_low": 1, "branch_high": 2}
            if protocol not in codes:
                raise ValueError(f"reset protocol must be one of {tuple(codes)}")
            self.P = P = P._replace(reset_protocol=codes[protocol])
            self._run_block = None
        k0 = int(k0)
        self.tick = k0
        self.k_reset = k0
        for a in (S.ring_float, S.ring_int, S.ring_int8, S.ring_bool, S.world_int, S.world_float, S.line_float, S.dp_fv,
                  S.dp_fr, S.dp_fm, S.th_x, S.th_g, S.th_u0, S.th_u1, S.junction, S.mo_sf, S.mo_si, S.mo_fx, S.mo_fc,
                  S.mo_fv, S.mo_fr, S.mo_fm, S.mo_samples, S.mo_ticks, S.ts_st, S.ts_fx, S.ts_fc, S.ts_primed, S.ts_fv,
                  S.ts_fr, S.ts_fm, S.ts_latest, S.ts_new, S.ts_sampled, S.rb_st, S.rb_fv, S.rb_fr, S.rb_fm,
                  S.pipe_vals, S.pipe_ticks, S.pipe_meta, S.sat, S.tune, S.fobs, S.fact, S.truth, S.truth_line,
                  S.las_wlo, S.las_whi, S.obs):
            a[...] = 0
        S.las_cache_j[...] = -1
        S.selfheat_float[...] = self._packed_f0
        # kernel caches keyed on their inputs — set keys that match nothing, so the first tick recomputes them
        S.ring_int[:, kernel.RI_HE_TCODE] = -1
        S.ring_int[:, kernel.RI_BI_TCODE] = -1
        S.line_float[:, kernel.LF_PDB_KEY] = np.nan
        S.world_float[:, kernel.WF_LOSS_KEY] = np.nan
        S.sc_cache[...] = self.scen_arrays.new_cache()
        # scenario values at k0 (signals without components keep their defaults)
        arr = self.scen_arrays
        out = arr.new_out()
        scen_eval(np.int64(k0), *arr.kernel_args(S.sc_cache), out)
        S.sc_v0[...] = out
        S.sc_v1[...] = out
        S.sc_vp[...] = out
        lay = arr.layout
        t_amb = out[:, lay["thermal.t_base_k"][0]] + out[:, lay["thermal.xpu_rise_k"][0]]
        S.world_float[:, kernel.WF_T_BASE0] = t_amb
        S.world_float[:, kernel.WF_T_BASE1] = t_amb
        S.th_t_obs[...] = t_amb[:, None]
        rf, ri = S.ring_float, S.ring_int
        for idx in (kernel.RF_T_RING, kernel.RF_T_HEATER, kernel.RF_T_BRANCH, kernel.RF_T_NEW, kernel.RF_T_PD):
            rf[:, idx, :] = t_amb[:, None]
        self._init_t_adc()
        # the scenario's ones density at k0 — a controller edge at k0 runs the bit-statistics window before the first interval sets RF_DENS (the window of the bits before k0, at the density sent at k0)
        o_dn = lay["data.ones_density"][0]
        rf[:, kernel.RF_DENS, :] = out[:, o_dn:o_dn + N]
        proto = int(P.reset_protocol)
        if proto in (0, 1):
            rf[:, kernel.RF_T_BRANCH, :] = -np.inf                  # the cold branch
        else:
            rf[:, kernel.RF_T_BRANCH, :] = np.inf                   # the hot branch
        S.ts_in[...] = t_amb[:, None] if S.ts_in.shape[1] else 0.0
        # heater DAC — registers, FIFO and drive at the initial code (default code_min)
        hp = self.heater_params
        code0 = np.full((B, N), hp.code_lo, np.int64) if heater_code is None else\
            np.clip(np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(heater_code, np.int64), (B, N)), hp.code_lo, hp.code_hi)
        ri[:, kernel.RI_HE_REG] = code0
        ri[:, kernel.RI_HE_PEND] = code0
        ri[:, kernel.RI_HE_LAST] = _NEVER
        S.he_fifo[...] = code0[:, :, None]
        u0 = np.zeros((B, N))
        rip = np.zeros((B, N))
        for b in range(B):
            electrical.heater_target_row(np.ascontiguousarray(code0[b]), int(P.he_law[b]), P.he_bits, P.he_pwm_bits,
                                         P.he_bit_err[b], P.he_bow[b], 0, 0, 1, u0[b], rip[b])
        rf[:, kernel.RF_HE_YS] = u0
        rf[:, kernel.RF_HE_YO] = u0
        rf[:, kernel.RF_HE_UT] = u0
        # bias DAC — the scenario's bias at k0 (or code 0 / the given code under controller ownership)
        bp = self.bias_params
        if bias_code is not None:
            bcode = np.clip(np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(bias_code, np.int64), (B, N)), 0, bp.code_max)
        elif P.bias_ctrl == 0:
            vs = out[:, lay["tx.bias_v"][0]:lay["tx.bias_v"][0] + N]
            vs = np.where(np.isfinite(vs), vs, P.bi_vmin)
            bcode = np.clip(np.rint((vs - P.bi_vmin) / ((P.bi_vmax - P.bi_vmin) / bp.code_max)), 0,
                            bp.code_max).astype(np.int64)
        else:
            bcode = np.zeros((B, N), np.int64)
        ri[:, kernel.RI_BI_REG] = bcode
        ri[:, kernel.RI_BI_PEND] = bcode
        ri[:, kernel.RI_BI_LAST] = _NEVER
        ri[:, kernel.RI_BI_CODE] = bcode
        S.bi_fifo[...] = bcode[:, :, None]
        v0 = np.zeros((B, N))
        for b in range(B):
            electrical.bias_target_row(np.ascontiguousarray(bcode[b]), P.bi_bits, P.bi_bit_err[b], P.bi_bow[b],
                                       P.bi_vmin[b], P.bi_vmax[b], v0[b])
        rf[:, kernel.RF_BI_YS] = v0
        rf[:, kernel.RF_BI_YO] = v0
        rf[:, kernel.RF_BI_VT] = v0
        rf[:, kernel.RF_BI_VAVG] = v0
        # data path — PRBS phases use tick-zero draws, matching DatapathBank.reset
        if P.dp_period > 0:
            for b in range(B):
                for n in range(N):
                    u = rng.uniform(P.dp_key_pat[b], n, 0, SLOT_PRBS_PHASE)
                    ri[b, kernel.RI_DP_BITPOS, n] = int(u * P.dp_period)
        # sensors — flags stay valid until a fault.
        # reset the fast-kernel cursor
        S.ring_bool[:, kernel.RB_MO_VALID, :] = True
        ri[:, kernel.RI_FAST_SEEN, :] = -1
        ri[:, kernel.RI_ASSIGN, :] = -1
        ri[:, kernel.RI_DECL, :] = P.ring_to_line[None, :]
        # held commands start from latched registers — mrm.control.api ABI rule
        S.act[...] = 0
        if self.maps.act_size:
            S.act[:, :self.maps.act_size] = self.maps.act_init
        # the registers of the non-DAC actuators start at their channel init values (they are the held command until the controller writes them)
        for i in range(self.maps.act_map.shape[0]):
            row = self.maps.act_map[i]
            dst, o, sz = int(row[AM_DST]), int(row[AM_OFFSET]), int(row[AM_SIZE])
            if dst == DST_HEATER:
                S.act[:, o:o + sz] = code0
            elif dst == DST_BIAS:
                S.act[:, o:o + sz] = bcode
            elif dst == DST_ASSIGN:
                ri[:, kernel.RI_ASSIGN] = S.act[:, o:o + sz]
            elif dst == DST_BS_THR:
                ri[:, kernel.RI_BS_THR] = S.act[:, o:o + sz]
            elif dst == DST_PGA:
                ri[:, kernel.RI_PGA] = S.act[:, o:o + sz]
            elif dst == DST_TUNE:
                S.tune[:, :sz] = S.act[:, o:o + sz]
        # first controller edge at or after k0
        per, ph0 = int(P.period), int(P.phase)
        j0 = 0 if k0 <= ph0 else -(-(k0 - ph0) // per)
        S.world_int[:, kernel.WI_EDGE_IDX] = j0
        for b in range(B):
            jitter_ticks = int(_edge_jitter_ticks(P, b, j0)) if P.jitter > 0 else 0
            S.world_int[b, kernel.WI_EDGE_NEXT] = ph0 + j0 * per + jitter_ticks
        S.world_int[:, kernel.WI_K_RESET] = k0
        S.world_int[:, kernel.WI_ORACLE_NEXT] = k0
        S.world_int[:, kernel.WI_PENDING_EDGE] = -1
        S.world_int[:, kernel.WI_SAT_FIRST_TICK] = -1  # no command clipped yet (on_out_of_range — error)
        # a bound compiled controller restarts from its post-init state (kept by bind_compiled. it is also what fault.controller_reset restores), so an episode after reset() repeats the first one exactly
        if self._ctrl is not None:
            S.ctrl_s_i64[...] = S.ctrl_s_i64_init
            S.ctrl_s_f64[...] = S.ctrl_s_f64_init
        self.metrics_state.reset(k0, code0)
        self.records_state.reset()
        self.validator.reset()
        self._pending = False

def _grow_pipeline(self) -> None:
        S = self.S
        B, capacity, n_actions = S.pipe_vals.shape
        queued_values = np.zeros((B, 2 * capacity, n_actions), np.int64)
        queued_ticks = np.zeros((B, 2 * capacity), np.int64)
        for b in range(B):
            head, count = int(S.pipe_meta[b, 0]), int(S.pipe_meta[b, 1])
            queue_indices = (head + np.arange(count)) % capacity
            queued_values[b, :count] = S.pipe_vals[b, queue_indices]
            queued_ticks[b, :count] = S.pipe_ticks[b, queue_indices]
            S.pipe_meta[b, 0] = 0
        self.S = S._replace(pipe_vals=queued_values, pipe_ticks=queued_ticks)
        self._caps["pipeline"] = 2 * capacity

def truth(self) -> Truth:
        S, P = self.S, self.P
        fields = {name: S.truth[:, i, :].copy() for i, name in enumerate(TRUTH_FIELDS)}
        out_rl = np.zeros((self.B, optics.RING_LINE_OUTPUT_ROW_COUNT, self.N, self.L))
        out_r = np.zeros((self.B, optics.RING_OUTPUT_ROW_COUNT, self.N))
        out_l = np.zeros((self.B, optics.LASER_LINE_OUTPUT_ROW_COUNT, self.L))
        for b in range(self.B):
            v = optics.unpack_self_heating_optical_state(S.selfheat_float[b], P.selfheat_int[b])
            out_rl[b], out_r[b], out_l[b] = (
                v[optics.SELF_HEATING_VIEW_INDEX_RING_LINE_OUTPUTS],
                v[optics.SELF_HEATING_VIEW_INDEX_RING_OUTPUTS],
                v[optics.SELF_HEATING_VIEW_INDEX_LASER_LINE_OUTPUTS],
            )
        return Truth(
            tick=int(self.tick),
            t_s=self.tick * self.dt,
            fields=fields,
            p_chip_w=S.truth_line[:, 0].copy(),
            p_out_w=S.truth_line[:, 1].copy(),
            lam_m=S.truth_line[:, 2].copy(),
            out_rl=out_rl,
            out_r=out_r,

def _per_ring_index(idx, N):
    indices = np.asarray(idx, np.int64).reshape(-1)
    if indices.size == N:

    ring_indices[:indices.size] = indices[:N]
    return ring_indices

nodes.name: solve_ring_temperature
nodes.meaning: one ring - the scalar solve
comments: one ring - the scalar solve
solve F(T) = T - T_other - g*P_abs(T) = 0 along the previous branch.
input - pabs_fn(T, k, packed_f, packed_i) returns P_abs (W) and dP_abs/dT (W/K)
input - k = k (1) - ring index
input - packed_f - callback parameters with units defined by the optical model
input - packed_i (1) - callback indices and offsets
input - t_other = T_other (K) - temperature without new same-ring optical heat
input - g = g (K/W) - absorbed-power response over this substep
input - t_start = T_prev (K) - previous root, or an infinite branch endpoint
input - p_max = P_max (W) - upper bound on non-negative absorption
input - d2p_max = max|d^2P_abs/dT^2| (W/K^2) - curvature bound
input - max_iter (1) - iteration limit
input - tol_k = epsilon_T (K) - residual or bracket tolerance
output - return[0] = T_next (K) - solved temperature
output - return[1] = P_abs(T_next) (W)
output - return[2] = dP_abs/dT(T_next) (W/K)
output - return[3] (1) - iteration count
output - return[4] (1) - STATUS_* result code
zero g returns t_other, and negative g mirrors the bounded interval.
roots lie between t_other and t_other + g*p_max when 0 <= P_abs <= p_max.
t_start=-infinity selects the cold endpoint, and +infinity selects the hot endpoint.
at most max_iter+1 optical evaluations include the starting point.
status 0 converges, 1 reaches max_iter, 2 violates the power bound, and 3 reports NaN gain.
let K2 = abs(g)*d2p_max (1/K).
d_min = 2*abs(F)/(F_prime + sqrt(F_prime^2 + 2*K2*abs(F))) (K).
with valid bounds, no root lies closer than d_min in the search direction.
this step approaches the first root and becomes Newton's step near a simple root.
without a positive curvature bound, safeguarded Newton can skip a root pair near a fold.
a limited iteration stays on the starting side of the root when the bounds are valid.

nodes.name: implicit_step_b
nodes.meaning: one implicit substep of the whole bank
comments: one implicit substep of the whole bank
advance one world's thermal state by one substep with implicit optical self-heating.
in place.

Thermal arrays (ThermalSystem.kernel_arrays() and ThermalSystem.coefficients(h)) - x, a, c0, c1 (M,) - lag_src, lag_obs, lag_kind (M,) - opt_lags (M_opt,) the LAG_OPT_SELF and LAG_OPT_OTHER lags - obs_ptr (O+1,) - src_ring (S,) - ring_obs (N,).
bus_order (N,) - ring indices in the order light reaches them.
u0, u1 (S,) W - exogenous source powers at the start and the end of the substep (held inputs - u1 = u0) - entries of waveguide-absorption sources are ignored.
src_scale (S,) - residue multipliers (1.0).
t_base K - base (package) temperature at the end of the substep.
p_prev (N,) W - the previous substep's absorbed power (drives the LAG_OPT_CROSS_RING lags).
t_prev (N,) K - the previous roots (branch continuation starts there).
pabs_fn returns (absorbed W, slope W/K).
commit_fn accepts (temperature K, ring, packed_f, packed_i).
p_max (N,) W and d2p_max (N,) W/K^2 bound
P_abs and |d2P_abs/dT2| for each ring (solve_ring_temperature).
n_outer >= 1 - bank sweeps. 1 = the cross-ring
optical heating lags one substep (valid while thermal.cross_optical_lag_gain < 0.05, e.g. for 1 us substeps).
n_outer > 1 repeats the bus-order sweep with the cross-ring lags driven by the newest P_abs (Gauss-Seidel), which makes the coupling implicit for long multi-tick steps.
the sweep stops early when P_abs no longer changes (1e-12 relative).
Scratch g_work (O,).
outputs - t_obs (O,) K end-of-step observer temperatures (absolute) - p_new (N,) W the absorbed power the thermal
state received (= P_abs(t_ring) when converged) - t_ring (N,) K the solved roots - n_iter (N,) iterations.
returns the number of rings whose solve did not converge (status 1, max_iter - 2, P_abs above p_max - or 3, a NaN gain).

Lag inputs - LAG_EXOGENOUS u0/u1 (exact FOH) - LAG_OPT_SELF P_abs,k(T_k) held over the step (implicit) - LAG_OPT_CROSS_RING p_prev (lagged one substep) - LAG_OPT_OTHER (heater resistor, PD, sensors) the new P_abs.
the ring observer of ring k ends equal to t_ring[k] (to rounding).
Cost - one pass over all lags, the ring solves, then one pass over the optical lags only.
for a single thermal pole, let a = exp(-h/tau) and G = residue*abs(dP_abs/dT) on the stable
negative-feedback flank.
explicit coupling has multiplier a-(1-a)*G.
it can alternate and diverge for fast poles — about -1.1 to -5.9 at h=1 us, tau=0.3–0.5 us, and G=1.2–7.
implicit coupling has multiplier a/(1+(1-a)*G), between zero and a for G>=0.
it avoids this numerical oscillation.
these are single-pole estimates when the model has several poles.
cross-ring optical heat uses the previous substep's power in a single outer sweep.
realization
checks its per-step gain and rejects values >=0.05.
additional outer sweeps make that coupling
implicit for longer steps.
this is distinct from the same-ring solve.
if a ring solve does not converge, the thermal state receives the power consistent with its returned temperature when that power can be recovered.
the next substep continues from this numerical result.
do not interpret iteration error as an additional physical thermal time constant.

source_ref.code:
@njit
def implicit_step_b(
    x,
    a,
    c0,
    c1,
    lag_src,
    lag_obs,
    lag_kind,
    opt_lags,
    obs_ptr,
    src_ring,
    ring_obs,
    bus_order,
    u0,
    u1,
    src_scale,
    t_base,
    p_prev,
    t_prev,
    pabs_fn,
    commit_fn,
    packed_f,
    packed_i,
    p_max,
    d2p_max,
    max_iter,
    tol_k,
    n_outer,
    g_work,
    t_obs,
    p_new,
    t_ring,
    n_iter,
):
    ring_count = ring_obs.shape[0]
    if bus_order.shape[0] != ring_count:
        raise ValueError("implicit_step: bus_order must list every ring once")
    for ring_index in range(ring_count):
        n_iter[ring_index] = 0
    for bus_position in range(ring_count):  # bus_order must be a permutation of 0..N-1 (n_iter as the marker)
        ring_index = bus_order[bus_position]
        if ring_index < 0 or ring_index >= ring_count or n_iter[ring_index] != 0:
            raise ValueError("implicit_step: bus_order must be a permutation of the ring indices")
        if ring_obs[ring_index] < 0:
            raise ValueError("implicit_step needs the ring_mode_weighted observer of every ring")
        n_iter[ring_index] = 1
    n_obs = obs_ptr.shape[0] - 1
    # advance every lag with its known input, then sum each observer.
    # Two passes give the same values and, per observer, the same summation order as one pass over the observers - the lag update without the sums is ~20 % faster.
    # LAG_OPT_SELF lags only decay here - their input is the unknown P_abs, and g_work collects their gain.
    for lag_index in range(lag_kind.shape[0]):
        source_index = lag_src[lag_index]
        lag_type = lag_kind[lag_index]
        lag_temperature_rise_k = a[lag_index] * x[lag_index]
        if lag_type == LAG_EXOGENOUS:
            lag_temperature_rise_k += src_scale[source_index] * (
                c0[lag_index] * u0[source_index] + c1[lag_index] * u1[source_index]
            )
        elif lag_type == LAG_OPT_CROSS_RING:
            lag_temperature_rise_k += (
                src_scale[source_index] * (c0[lag_index] + c1[lag_index]) * p_prev[src_ring[source_index]]
            )
        x[lag_index] = lag_temperature_rise_k
    for observer_index in range(n_obs):
        known_observer_temp_k = t_base
        self_heating_gain_k_per_w = 0.0
        for lag_index in range(obs_ptr[observer_index], obs_ptr[observer_index + 1]):
            if lag_kind[lag_index] == LAG_OPT_SELF:
                self_heating_gain_k_per_w += src_scale[lag_src[lag_index]] * (c0[lag_index] + c1[lag_index])
            known_observer_temp_k += x[lag_index]
        t_obs[observer_index] = known_observer_temp_k  # everything except the new optical inputs
        g_work[observer_index] = self_heating_gain_k_per_w
    failed_ring_count = 0
    cross_ring_absorbed_power_w = np.empty(ring_count)  # P_abs currently driving the LAG_OPT_CROSS_RING lags
    for ring_index in range(ring_count):
        cross_ring_absorbed_power_w[ring_index] = p_prev[ring_index]
        t_ring[ring_index] = t_prev[ring_index]
        n_iter[ring_index] = 0
    for sweep in range(max(n_outer, 1)):
        failed_ring_count = 0
        for bus_position in range(ring_count):
            ring_index = bus_order[bus_position]
            observer_index = ring_obs[ring_index]
            if observer_index < 0:
                raise ValueError("implicit_step needs the ring_mode_weighted observer of every ring")
            (
                solved_temp_k,
                solved_absorbed_power_w,
                d_solved_power_dtemp_w_per_k,
                iterations_used,
                solve_status,
            ) = solve_ring_temperature(
                pabs_fn,
                ring_index,
                packed_f,
                packed_i,
                t_obs[observer_index],
                g_work[observer_index],
                t_ring[ring_index],
                p_max[ring_index],
                d2p_max[ring_index],
                max_iter,
                tol_k,
            )
            t_ring[ring_index] = solved_temp_k
            p_new[ring_index] = solved_absorbed_power_w
            n_iter[ring_index] += iterations_used
            if solve_status != STATUS_CONVERGED:
                failed_ring_count += 1
                # a branch jump can need more than max_iter steps, or p_max can fail to bound absorption.
                # feed the thermal state with power consistent with the returned temperature.
                # with valid bounds, that point stays before the root, and the next substep continues from it.
                # a NaN gain keeps P_abs at the returned point (no such power exists).
                ring_self_heating_gain_k_per_w = g_work[observer_index]
                if ring_self_heating_gain_k_per_w != 0.0 and solve_status != STATUS_NAN_GAIN:
                    p_new[ring_index] = (
                        solved_temp_k - t_obs[observer_index]
                    ) / ring_self_heating_gain_k_per_w
            commit_fn(solved_temp_k, ring_index, packed_f, packed_i)
        if sweep + 1 >= n_outer:
            break
        # Gauss-Seidel - drive the cross-ring lags with the newest P_abs, then sweep again
        max_power_change_w = 0.0
        max_absorbed_power_w = 0.0
        for ring_index in range(ring_count):
            max_power_change_w = max(
                max_power_change_w, abs(p_new[ring_index] - cross_ring_absorbed_power_w[ring_index])
            )
            max_absorbed_power_w = max(max_absorbed_power_w, abs(p_new[ring_index]))
        if max_power_change_w <= 1e-12 * max_absorbed_power_w:
            break
        for lag_index in range(lag_kind.shape[0]):
            if lag_kind[lag_index] == LAG_OPT_CROSS_RING:
                source_index = lag_src[lag_index]
                source_ring_index = src_ring[source_index]
                lag_temperature_change_k = (
                    src_scale[source_index]
                    * (c0[lag_index] + c1[lag_index])
                    * (p_new[source_ring_index] - cross_ring_absorbed_power_w[source_ring_index])
                )
                x[lag_index] += lag_temperature_change_k
                t_obs[lag_obs[lag_index]] += lag_temperature_change_k
        for ring_index in range(ring_count):
            cross_ring_absorbed_power_w[ring_index] = p_new[ring_index]
    for i in range(opt_lags.shape[0]):
        lag_index = opt_lags[i]
        source_index = lag_src[lag_index]
        lag_temperature_change_k = (
            src_scale[source_index] * (c0[lag_index] + c1[lag_index]) * p_new[src_ring[source_index]]
        )
        x[lag_index] += lag_temperature_change_k
        t_obs[lag_obs[lag_index]] += lag_temperature_change_k
    return failed_ring_count

@njit
def implicit_step(x, a, c0, c1, lag_src, lag_obs, lag_kind, opt_lags, obs_ptr, src_ring, ring_obs, bus_order,
                  u0, u1, src_scale, t_base, p_prev, t_prev,
                  pabs_fn, commit_fn, packed_f, packed_i, p_max, d2p_max, max_iter, tol_k, n_outer,
                  g_work, t_obs, p_new, t_ring, n_iter):
    B = x.shape[0]
    for n in (a.shape[0], c0.shape[0], c1.shape[0], u0.shape[0], u1.shape[0], src_scale.shape[0], t_base.shape[0],
              packed_f.shape[0], packed_i.shape[0], p_max.shape[0], d2p_max.shape[0]):
        if n != 1 and n != B:
            raise ValueError("implicit_step: every per-world input must have 1 or B rows")
    if c0.shape[0] != a.shape[0] or c1.shape[0] != a.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("implicit_step: a, c0, c1 must have the same rows")
    for n in (p_prev.shape[0], t_prev.shape[0], g_work.shape[0], t_obs.shape[0], p_new.shape[0], t_ring.shape[0],
              n_iter.shape[0]):
        if n != B:
            raise ValueError("implicit_step: p_prev, t_prev and the work/output arrays must have B rows")
    n_fail = 0
    for b in range(x.shape[0]):
        ra = shared_or_world_row_index(b, a.shape[0])
        n_fail += implicit_step_b(
            x[b], a[ra], c0[ra], c1[ra], lag_src, lag_obs, lag_kind, opt_lags, obs_ptr, src_ring, ring_obs, bus_order,
            u0[shared_or_world_row_index(b, u0.shape[0])], u1[shared_or_world_row_index(b, u1.shape[0])], src_scale[shared_or_world_row_index(b, src_scale.shape[0])],
            t_base[shared_or_world_row_index(b, t_base.shape[0])], p_prev[b], t_prev[b], pabs_fn, commit_fn,
            packed_f[shared_or_world_row_index(b, packed_f.shape[0])], packed_i[shared_or_world_row_index(b, packed_i.shape[0])],
            p_max[shared_or_world_row_index(b, p_max.shape[0])], d2p_max[shared_or_world_row_index(b, d2p_max.shape[0])], max_iter, tol_k, n_outer,
            g_work[b], t_obs[b], p_new[b], t_ring[b], n_iter[b])
    return n_fail

@njit
def implicit_run_b(x, a, c0, c1, lag_src, lag_obs, lag_kind, opt_lags, obs_ptr, src_ring, ring_obs, bus_order,
                   u_steps, t_base_steps, src_scale, p_prev, t_prev,
                   pabs_fn, commit_fn, packed_f, packed_i, p_max, d2p_max, max_iter, tol_k, n_outer,
                   t_ring_hist, p_hist, t_obs_hist):
    n_steps = u_steps.shape[0]
    n_obs = obs_ptr.shape[0] - 1
    n_rings = ring_obs.shape[0]
    g_work = np.zeros(n_obs)
    p_new = np.zeros(n_rings)
    t_ring = np.zeros(n_rings)
    n_iter = np.zeros(n_rings, np.int64)
    failure_count = 0
    for i in range(n_steps):
        failure_count += implicit_step_b(x, a, c0, c1, lag_src, lag_obs, lag_kind, opt_lags, obs_ptr, src_ring,
            ring_obs,
                                 bus_order, u_steps[i], u_steps[i], src_scale, t_base_steps[i], p_prev, t_prev,
                                 pabs_fn, commit_fn, packed_f, packed_i, p_max, d2p_max, max_iter, tol_k, n_outer,
                                 g_work, t_obs_hist[i], p_new, t_ring, n_iter)
        for k in range(n_rings):
            p_prev[k] = p_new[k]
            t_prev[k] = t_ring[k]
            t_ring_hist[i, k] = t_ring[k]
            p_hist[i, k] = p_new[k]
    return failure_count

nodes.name: pabs_lorentzian
nodes.meaning: built-in Lorentzian absorption (packed arguments)
comments: built-in Lorentzian absorption (packed arguments)
sum Lorentzian absorption and its temperature derivative for one ring.
input - t = T (K) - trial temperature
input - k = k (1) - ring index
input - packed_f - mixed-unit LZ_* parameters defined above
input - packed_i (1) - ring count and parameter offsets
output - absorbed_power_w = P_abs(T) (W)
output - d_absorbed_power_dtemp_w_per_k = dP_abs/dT (W/K)
lambda_r = lambda_ref + s0*(dT + beta*dT^2/2), with dT = T-T_ref (K).
for each line, u = (lambda_r-lambda_line)/HWHM (1).
P_abs = sum(p_peak/(1+u^2)).
include dlambda_r/dT = s0*(1+beta*dT) (m/K) in the derivative.
this study model uses the TCMT Lorentzian limit.

source_ref.code:
@njit
def pabs_lorentzian(t, k, packed_f, packed_i):
    ring_offset = packed_i[1 + k]
    reference_wavelength_m = packed_f[ring_offset + LZ_LAM_REF]
    reference_temp_k = packed_f[ring_offset + LZ_T_REF]
    reference_tuning_slope_m_per_k = packed_f[ring_offset + LZ_S0]
    relative_tuning_curvature_per_k = packed_f[ring_offset + LZ_BETA]
    n_lines = int(packed_f[ring_offset + LZ_N_LINES])
    temp_change_k = t - reference_temp_k
    resonance_m = reference_wavelength_m + reference_tuning_slope_m_per_k * (
        temp_change_k + 0.5 * relative_tuning_curvature_per_k * temp_change_k * temp_change_k
    )
    tuning_slope_m_per_k = reference_tuning_slope_m_per_k * (
        1.0 + relative_tuning_curvature_per_k * temp_change_k
    )
    absorbed_power_w = 0.0
    d_absorbed_power_dtemp_w_per_k = 0.0
    for line_index in range(n_lines):
        line_offset = ring_offset + LZ_HEADER + LZ_PER_LINE * line_index
        half_linewidth_m = packed_f[line_offset + LZ_LINE_HWHM]
        detuning_in_half_widths = (resonance_m - packed_f[line_offset + LZ_LINE_LAM]) / half_linewidth_m
        denominator = 1.0 + detuning_in_half_widths * detuning_in_half_widths
        peak_absorbed_w = packed_f[line_offset + LZ_LINE_PEAK]
        absorbed_power_w += peak_absorbed_w / denominator
        d_absorbed_power_dtemp_w_per_k -= (
            peak_absorbed_w
            * 2.0
            * detuning_in_half_widths
            / (denominator * denominator)
            / half_linewidth_m
            * tuning_slope_m_per_k
        )
    return absorbed_power_w, d_absorbed_power_dtemp_w_per_k

def pack_lorentzian_args(lam_ref_m, t_ref_k, s0_m_per_k, beta_per_k, lam_line_m, hwhm_m, p_peak_w):
    lp = np.asarray(p_peak_w, np.float64)
    if lp.ndim == 1:
        lp = lp[None, :, None]
    elif lp.ndim == 2:
        lp = lp[None]
    B0, N, L = lp.shape
    per_ring = [np.asarray(v, np.float64) for v in (lam_ref_m, t_ref_k, s0_m_per_k, beta_per_k)]
    per_line = [np.asarray(v, np.float64) for v in (lam_line_m, hwhm_m)]
    # batch rows - only the leading axis of a (B, N) per-ring or (B, N, L) per-line array counts (np.atleast_3d would turn an (N, L) array into (N, L, 1) and take N for B)
    B = max([B0] + [v.shape[0] for v in per_ring if v.ndim == 2] + [v.shape[0] for v in per_line if v.ndim == 3])

    # a per-ring array broadcast to (B, N).
    def to_rings(v):
        return np.broadcast_to(np.atleast_2d(v) if v.ndim < 2 else v, (B, N))

    # a per-(ring, line) array broadcast to (B, N, L) - a 1-D array is per ring.
    def to_lines(v):
        v = v if v.ndim == 3 else (v[None] if v.ndim == 2 else np.reshape(v, (1, -1, 1) if v.ndim == 1 else (1, 1, 1)))
        return np.broadcast_to(v, (B, N, L))

    lam_ref, t_ref, s0, beta = (to_rings(v) for v in per_ring)
    lam_l, hw = (to_lines(v) for v in per_line)
    pk = np.broadcast_to(lp, (B, N, L))
    if np.any(hw <= 0):
        raise ValueError("HWHM must be > 0")
    block = LZ_HEADER + LZ_PER_LINE * L
    packed_f = np.zeros((B, N * block))
    packed_i = np.zeros((B, 1 + N), np.int64)
    packed_i[:, 0] = N
    for k in range(N):
        off = k * block
        packed_i[:, 1 + k] = off
        packed_f[:, off + LZ_LAM_REF] = lam_ref[:, k]
        packed_f[:, off + LZ_T_REF] = t_ref[:, k]
        packed_f[:, off + LZ_S0] = s0[:, k]
        packed_f[:, off + LZ_BETA] = beta[:, k]
        packed_f[:, off + LZ_N_LINES] = L
        for l in range(L):
            j = off + LZ_HEADER + LZ_PER_LINE * l
            packed_f[:, j + LZ_LINE_LAM] = lam_l[:, k, l]
            packed_f[:, j + LZ_LINE_HWHM] = hw[:, k, l]
            packed_f[:, j + LZ_LINE_PEAK] = pk[:, k, l]
    return packed_f, packed_i

comments: bound absorption and its first two temperature derivatives over all laser lines.
input - p_peak_w = P_peak (W) - peak absorption per ring and line
input - hwhm_m = gamma_lambda (m) - half width at half maximum
input - s0_m_per_k = s_0 (m/K) - reference thermal tuning slope
input - beta_per_k = beta (1/K) - relative slope curvature
input - dt_max_k = max|T-T_ref| (K) - assumed temperature excursion bound
output - absorbed_power_bound_w = P_max (W) - bound on absorbed power
output - power_temp_derivative_bound_w_per_k = max|dP_abs/dT| (W/K) - slope bound
output - power_temp_curvature_bound_w_per_k2 = max|d^2P_abs/dT^2| (W/K^2) - curvature bound
line arrays have shape (..., N, L), and tuning arrays broadcast to (..., N).
with u=(lambda_r-lambda_L)/gamma_lambda, max|dP/du|=(3*sqrt(3)/8)*P_peak.
max|d^2P/du^2|=2*P_peak, and |dlambda_r/dT| <= |s_0|*(1+|beta|*dt_max_k).
sum line bounds to bound the full absorption curve.
the default 200 K excursion is an assumed margin, not a solved temperature.
dmax checks cross-ring lag gain, and d2max safeguards the temperature solve.

source_ref.code:
def lorentzian_bounds(p_peak_w, hwhm_m, s0_m_per_k, beta_per_k=0.0, dt_max_k=200.0):
    peak_absorbed_power_w = np.asarray(p_peak_w, np.float64)
    half_linewidth_m = np.asarray(hwhm_m, np.float64)
    abs_tuning_slope_m_per_k = np.abs(np.asarray(s0_m_per_k, np.float64))
    abs_relative_tuning_curvature_per_k = np.abs(np.asarray(beta_per_k, np.float64))
    tuning_slope_bound_m_per_k = abs_tuning_slope_m_per_k * (
        1.0 + abs_relative_tuning_curvature_per_k * float(dt_max_k)
    )
    absorbed_power_bound_w = peak_absorbed_power_w.sum(axis=-1)
    power_temp_derivative_bound_w_per_k = (LORENTZ_MAX_SLOPE * peak_absorbed_power_w / half_linewidth_m).sum(
        axis=-1
    ) * tuning_slope_bound_m_per_k
    power_temp_curvature_bound_w_per_k2 = (2.0 * peak_absorbed_power_w / half_linewidth_m**2).sum(
        axis=-1
    ) * tuning_slope_bound_m_per_k**2 + (LORENTZ_MAX_SLOPE * peak_absorbed_power_w / half_linewidth_m).sum(
        axis=-1
    ) * abs_tuning_slope_m_per_k * abs_relative_tuning_curvature_per_k
    return absorbed_power_bound_w, power_temp_derivative_bound_w_per_k, power_temp_curvature_bound_w_per_k2

comments: analytic results of the single-line problem (test targets)
Compact-model notes, section 6.4.
the self-heating tests check the solver against these closed forms.
find folds of y = y_o + A/(1+y^2) for one laser line.
input - A = G_sh*P_peak/HWHM (1) - optical heating strength
output - return[0] = y_a (1) - lower normalized resonance detuning

output - return[3] = y_o,b (1) - decreasing-heater fold
y = (lambda_r-lambda_L)/HWHM (1), and y_o excludes optical heating.

increasing heater input jumps at y_o,a, and decreasing input jumps at y_o,b.
return None when A <= 8/(3*sqrt(3)) or no fold pair is found.

def step(self, h_s, u0, u1, t_base_k, pabs_fn, packed_f, packed_i, p_max, d2p_max, *, commit_fn=commit_none,
             bus_order=None, src_scale=None, max_iter: int = 10, tol_k: float = 1e-9, n_outer: int = 1) -> int:
        thermal_system = self.system
        if self._h != h_s:
            self._coef = thermal_system.coefficients(h_s)
            self._h = h_s
        a, c0, c1 = self._coef
        ring_bus_order = np.arange(thermal_system.n_rings,
            dtype=np.int64) if bus_order is None else np.asarray(bus_order, np.int64)
        source_scales = (
            np.ones((1, thermal_system.n_src)) if src_scale is None
            else np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(src_scale, np.float64))
        )
        failure_count = implicit_step(self.x, a, c0, c1, thermal_system.lag_src, thermal_system.lag_obs,
            thermal_system.lag_kind, thermal_system.opt_lags, thermal_system.obs_ptr, thermal_system.src_ring,
                           thermal_system.ring_obs, ring_bus_order,
                           np.atleast_2d(u0), np.atleast_2d(u1), source_scales, np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(t_base_k,
                               np.float64)),
                           self.p_prev, self.t_prev, pabs_fn, commit_fn, np.atleast_2d(packed_f),
                           np.atleast_2d(packed_i), np.atleast_2d(p_max), np.atleast_2d(d2p_max), max_iter, tol_k,
                           n_outer, self.g_work, self.t_obs, self.p_new, self.t_ring, self.n_iter)
        self.p_prev[:] = self.p_new
        self.t_prev[:] = self.t_ring
        return int(failure_count)

@njit(cache=True, _nrt=False)
def flicker_step(key, ring, tick, slot0, coef, fx, fc):
    sample_contribution = 0.0
    for j in range(coef.shape[0]):
        z1, z2 = rng.normal2(key, ring, tick, slot0 + j)
        previous_ou_value = fx[j]
        previous_contribution = fc[j]
        next_ou_value = (
            coef[j, _FL_P00] * previous_ou_value + coef[j, _FL_P01] * previous_contribution + coef[j, _FL_L00] * z1
        )
        next_contribution = (
            coef[j, _FL_P10] * previous_ou_value + coef[j, _FL_P11] * previous_contribution
            + coef[j, _FL_L10] * z1 + coef[j, _FL_L11] * z2
        )
        fx[j] = next_ou_value
        fc[j] = next_contribution
        sample_contribution += next_contribution
    return sample_contribution

nodes.name: monitor_tick_row
nodes.meaning: monitor kernels
comments: monitor kernels
Integrate plant interval [k, k+1) for the N monitor channels of one world, then take, convert and queue the samples whose sample tick is k + 1.
i_dark_in (N,), optional - the PD dark currents dark_current_a(pw[PW_DARK_I0], t_pd_k, pw[PW_DARK_T0], pw[PW_DARK_EA]) already computed by the caller (the engine shares them with Truth).
inputs have shape (N,).
p_pd_w (W) sums drop-port power over all lines and orders.
p_bg_w (W) is the bus power used for background pickup.
t_pd_k (K) is the monitor_pd observer temperature.
t_adc_k (K) is the selected ADC reference-site temperature.
MonitorHw.adc_temperature selects the PD observer or package base.
pga_sel is a clipped int64 PGA index, and fault is an int8 FAULT_* mask.

Parameters - pr (N, NPR), pw (NPW,), lat (ADC latency, ticks), phase (N,) sample phases (ticks, adc_mux), pga_gains (G,) (empty = gain 1), fl_coef (J, N_FLICKER_COEF) flicker coefficients (J = 0 - no flicker).

Switches - afe_type (AFE_*), window_ticks W, period_ticks P (W <= P), code_max = 2^bits - 1, shot_on, stuck_flagged (a stuck converter marks its samples invalid), slot_base (counter-RNG slot offset of this bank).

Keys (uint64) - key_adc (TIA + flicker, noise seed), key_shot (shot noise, noise seed), key_dnl (DNL, device seed - the thresholds are keyed by the ring's converter pr[n, PR_ADC_UNIT], so rings that share a converter share them).
State - sf (N, NSF), si (N, NSI), fx/fc (N, J), FIFO fv/fr/fm (N, C) (mrm.core.timing).
out_sampled (N,) int8 - 0 no sample, 1 sample queued, 2 sample lost because the FIFO was full.
for an integrate-and-dump mean, accumulate S_k/2 and draw once at the sample.
variance equals
sum(S_k/2)*dt/(n*dt)^2.
constant S gives S/(2*window_s).
for an RC filter with mu = 1/tau, a = exp(-mu*dt), each tick adds variance (S*mu/4)*(1-a^2).
carry the noise state across samples
and decay its accumulated variance exactly.
stationary variance is S/(4*tau).
these updates use the filter's discrete covariance, rather than a guessed noise bandwidth.

@njit(cache=True, _nrt=False)
def monitor_tick_row(
    k,
    p_pd_w,
    p_bg_w,
    t_pd_k,
    t_adc_k,
    pga_sel,
    fault,
    pr,
    pw,
    lat,
    phase,
    pga_gains,
    fl_coef,
    afe_type,
    window_ticks,
    period_ticks,
    code_max,
    shot_on,
    stuck_flagged,
    slot_base,
    key_adc,
    key_shot,
    key_dnl,
    sf,
    si,
    fx,
    fc,
    fv,
    fr,
    fm,
    out_sampled,
    i_dark_in=None,
):
    n_rings = p_pd_w.shape[0]
    n_pga = pga_gains.shape[0]
    gain_scale = pw[PW_GAIN_SCALE]
    dark_reference_a = pw[PW_DARK_I0]
    dark_reference_k = pw[PW_DARK_T0]
    dark_activation_j = pw[PW_DARK_EA]
    tia_noise_psd_a2_per_hz = pw[PW_S_TIA]  # TIA white noise PSD, one-sided A^2/Hz
    rc_state_retention = pw[PW_A_TICK]  # rc - exp(-dt/tau)
    rc_decay_rate_per_s = pw[PW_MU]  # rc - 1/tau, 1/s
    tick_duration_s = pw[PW_DT]
    rc_variance_injection_fraction = 1.0 - rc_state_retention * rc_state_retention
    for n in range(n_rings):
        out_sampled[n] = 0
        signal_current_a = gain_scale * pr[n, PR_RESP] * (p_pd_w[n] + pr[n, PR_BG] * p_bg_w[n])
        if i_dark_in is None:
            photodiode_dark_current_a = dark_current_a(
                dark_reference_a, t_pd_k[n], dark_reference_k, dark_activation_j
            )
        else:
            photodiode_dark_current_a = i_dark_in[n]
        total_current_a = signal_current_a + photodiode_dark_current_a
        # one-sided shot-noise PSD in A^2/Hz
        shot_noise_psd_a2_per_hz = (
            2.0 * Q_E * (abs(signal_current_a) + photodiode_dark_current_a) if shot_on else 0.0
        )
        sample_tick = next_edge(k + 1, period_ticks, phase[n])  # next sample tick (>= k + 1)
        if si[n, _SI_PRIMED] == 0:
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_I] = 0.0
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_TICKS] = 0.0
            sf[n, _SF_Y_SIGNAL] = total_current_a  # rc - start in steady state
            sf[n, _SF_Y_SHOT] = 0.0
            sf[n, _SF_Y_TIA] = 0.0
            sf[n, _SF_DECAY] = 1.0
            if afe_type == AFE_RC:  # stationary start - accumulated variance = S/(4 tau)
                sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_SHOT] = 0.25 * shot_noise_psd_a2_per_hz * rc_decay_rate_per_s
                sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_TIA] = 0.25 * tia_noise_psd_a2_per_hz * rc_decay_rate_per_s
            else:
                sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_SHOT] = 0.0
                sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_TIA] = 0.0
            if fl_coef.shape[0] > 0:
                _flicker_init(key_adc, n, k, slot_base + _SLOT_FL_INIT, fl_coef, fx[n], fc[n])
            si[n, _SI_PRIMED] = 1
        if afe_type == AFE_INTEGRATE_DUMP:
            if k >= sample_tick - window_ticks:  # this interval is inside the window of the sample
                sf[n, _SF_ACC_I] += total_current_a
                sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_SHOT] += 0.5 * shot_noise_psd_a2_per_hz
                sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_TIA] += 0.5 * tia_noise_psd_a2_per_hz
                sf[n, _SF_ACC_TICKS] += 1.0
        else:
            sf[n, _SF_Y_SIGNAL] = (
                rc_state_retention * sf[n, _SF_Y_SIGNAL] + (1.0 - rc_state_retention) * total_current_a
            )  # exact for a ZOH input
            sf[n, _SF_DECAY] *= rc_state_retention
            # decayed variance since the last sample - the discrete Gramian of the RC filter
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_SHOT] = (
                rc_state_retention * rc_state_retention * sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_SHOT]
                + 0.25 * shot_noise_psd_a2_per_hz * rc_decay_rate_per_s * rc_variance_injection_fraction
            )
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_TIA] = (
                rc_state_retention * rc_state_retention * sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_TIA]
                + 0.25 * tia_noise_psd_a2_per_hz * rc_decay_rate_per_s * rc_variance_injection_fraction
            )
        if k + 1 != sample_tick:
            continue
        # take the sample - filtered_current_a is the front-end output current in A
        tia_noise_draw = rng.normal(key_adc, n, sample_tick, slot_base + _SLOT_WHITE)
        shot_noise_draw = rng.normal(key_shot, n, sample_tick, slot_base) if shot_on else 0.0
        if afe_type == AFE_INTEGRATE_DUMP:
            window_count = sf[n, _SF_ACC_TICKS]
            if window_count < 1.0:
                window_count = 1.0
            filtered_current_a = sf[n, _SF_ACC_I] / window_count
            # window-mean noise - Var = sum_k (S_k/2) dt / (m dt)^2 = acc / (m^2 dt)
            filtered_current_a += (
                math.sqrt(sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_SHOT] / (window_count * window_count * tick_duration_s))
                * shot_noise_draw
                + math.sqrt(sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_TIA] / (window_count * window_count * tick_duration_s))
                * tia_noise_draw
            )
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_I] = 0.0
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_SHOT] = 0.0
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_TIA] = 0.0
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_TICKS] = 0.0
        else:
            shot_current_a = (
                sf[n, _SF_DECAY] * sf[n, _SF_Y_SHOT] + math.sqrt(sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_SHOT]) * shot_noise_draw
            )
            tia_current_a = (
                sf[n, _SF_DECAY] * sf[n, _SF_Y_TIA] + math.sqrt(sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_TIA]) * tia_noise_draw
            )
            sf[n, _SF_Y_SHOT] = shot_current_a
            sf[n, _SF_Y_TIA] = tia_current_a
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_SHOT] = 0.0
            sf[n, _SF_ACC_VAR_TIA] = 0.0
            sf[n, _SF_DECAY] = 1.0
            filtered_current_a = sf[n, _SF_Y_SIGNAL] + shot_current_a + tia_current_a
        if fl_coef.shape[0] > 0:
            filtered_current_a += flicker_step(
                key_adc, n, sample_tick, slot_base + _SLOT_FLICKER, fl_coef, fx[n], fc[n]
            )
        # subtract the analog baseline, select PGA gain, and convert to ADC codes
        filtered_current_a -= pr[n, PR_IBASE]
        pga_gain = 1.0
        if n_pga > 0:
            sel = pga_sel[n]
            if sel < 0:
                sel = 0
            elif sel > n_pga - 1:
                sel = n_pga - 1
            pga_gain = pga_gains[sel]
        reference_gain_factor = 1.0 + pw[PW_TEMPCO] * (
            t_adc_k[n] - pw[PW_T_REF]
        )  # reference drift with its temperature
        ideal_code = (
            filtered_current_a * pga_gain / pw[PW_LSB] * (1.0 + pr[n, PR_GAIN_ERR]) / reference_gain_factor
            + pr[n, PR_OFFSET]
        )
        code, over = adc_quantize(
            ideal_code,
            pr[n, PR_INL_BOW],
            pw[PW_DNL],
            code_max,
            key_dnl,
            np.int64(pr[n, PR_ADC_UNIT]),
            slot_base,
        )
        flags = SAMPLE_OVERRANGE if over else 0
        fault_n = fault[n]
        if fault_n & FAULT_ADC_SATURATE:
            code = np.int64(code_max)
            flags |= SAMPLE_OVERRANGE
        if fault_n & FAULT_ADC_STUCK:
            # the frozen converter reports its last good code - the clip state of the hidden conversion is not seen
            code = si[n, _SI_LAST_CODE]
            flags = SAMPLE_INVALID if stuck_flagged else 0
        if fault_n & FAULT_ADC_DROP:
            flags |= SAMPLE_INVALID | SAMPLE_DROPPED
        if not (fault_n & (FAULT_ADC_STUCK | FAULT_ADC_DROP)):
            si[n, _SI_LAST_CODE] = code
        # queue the sample for release at sample tick + ADC latency
        sample_queued = fifo_push(
            fv, fr, fm, n, code | (np.int64(flags) << SAMPLE_FLAG_SHIFT), sample_tick + lat
        )
        out_sampled[n] = 1 if sample_queued else 2

release tick equals sample tick plus lat.
out_samples and out_ticks have shape (N, M).
each ring's first out_count entries are valid and ordered by sample tick.
later entries are zero.
latest holds the previous code until at least one non-dropped sample arrives.
out_valid is false if any released sample was invalid, including a dropped or flagged stuck sample.
out_over marks clipping or forced saturation among non-dropped samples.
out_new marks at least one delivered code.
these flags describe this release, not the held latest value's full history.

@njit(cache=True, _nrt=False)
def monitor_release_row(now, lat, fv, fr, fm, out_samples, out_ticks, out_count, latest, out_valid, out_over,
                        out_new):
    n_rings = fm.shape[0]
    sample_capacity = out_samples.shape[1]
    discarded_samples = 0
    for n in range(n_rings):
        sample_count = 0
        valid = True
        over = False
        while True:
            sample_ready, packed_sample, release_tick = fifo_pop_ready(fv, fr, fm, n, now)
            if not sample_ready:
                break
            flags = packed_sample >> SAMPLE_FLAG_SHIFT
            code = packed_sample & SAMPLE_CODE_MASK
            if flags & SAMPLE_INVALID:
                valid = False
            if flags & SAMPLE_DROPPED:      # a lost sample - no code and no clip flag reach the controller
                continue
            if flags & SAMPLE_OVERRANGE:
                over = True
            if sample_count == sample_capacity:
                for m in range(sample_capacity - 1):
                    out_samples[n, m] = out_samples[n, m + 1]
                    out_ticks[n, m] = out_ticks[n, m + 1]
                sample_count = sample_capacity - 1
                discarded_samples += 1
            out_samples[n, sample_count] = code
            out_ticks[n, sample_count] = release_tick - lat
            sample_count += 1
        for m in range(sample_count, sample_capacity):
            out_samples[n, m] = 0
            out_ticks[n, m] = 0
        out_count[n] = sample_count
        if sample_count > 0:
            latest[n] = out_samples[n, sample_count - 1]
        out_valid[n] = valid
        out_over[n] = over
        out_new[n] = sample_count > 0
    return discarded_samples

nodes.name: monitor_level_codes_row
nodes.meaning: Ideal monitor codes of the two NRZ levels and their noise, for a bit-rate sampler (the bit statistics).
comments: Ideal monitor codes of the two NRZ levels and their noise, for a bit-rate sampler (the bit statistics).
mu_x = the ADC transfer of i_x = gain_scale R (P_x + f_bg P_bus) + i_d (without quantization, INL or DNL) -
sigma_x^2 = (2 q (i_sig,x + i_d) [shot_on] + S_tia) / (4 tau_s) in A^2 - the exact variance of an instantaneous
sample of white noise through a single-pole sampler front end of time constant tau_s (= 1/(2 pi f_3dB) - 1/(4 tau) is the noise bandwidth of one pole), converted to codes with the same gain as mu.
tau_s is a property of the sampler hardware (datapath.bitstat_bw_hz), not of the plant step.
Flicker is not included (it is far slower than one bit-statistics window).
S_tia is the monitor's input noise density pw[PW_S_TIA] unless s_tia_a2_per_hz >= 0 is given - a bit-rate front end is a different, wider-band amplifier (its noise density is assumed, no data).
rin_per_hz (1/Hz) is one-sided laser relative-intensity noise and defaults to zero.
it adds (gain_scale*R*P_x)^2*RIN/(4*tau_s) at the sampler bandwidth.
per-tick laser RIN changes levels only at the tick rate.
the bit-rate sampler sees the RIN band up to its own bandwidth.
exclude background light from this term.

@njit(cache=True, _nrt=False)
def monitor_level_codes_row(
    p1_w,
    p0_w,
    p_bg_w,
    t_pd_k,
    t_adc_k,
    pga_sel,
    pr,
    pw,
    pga_gains,
    shot_on,
    tau_s,
    out_mu1,
    out_mu0,
    out_sig1,
    out_sig0,
    s_tia_a2_per_hz=-1.0,
    rin_per_hz=0.0,
):
    n_rings = p1_w.shape[0]
    n_pga = pga_gains.shape[0]
    tia_noise_psd_a2_per_hz = pw[PW_S_TIA] if s_tia_a2_per_hz < 0.0 else s_tia_a2_per_hz
    for n in range(n_rings):
        pga_gain = 1.0
        if n_pga > 0:
            sel = pga_sel[n]
            if sel < 0:
                sel = 0
            elif sel > n_pga - 1:
                sel = n_pga - 1
            pga_gain = pga_gains[sel]
        reference_gain_factor = 1.0 + pw[PW_TEMPCO] * (t_adc_k[n] - pw[PW_T_REF])
        codes_per_ampere = pga_gain / pw[PW_LSB] * (1.0 + pr[n, PR_GAIN_ERR]) / reference_gain_factor
        photodiode_dark_current_a = dark_current_a(pw[PW_DARK_I0], t_pd_k[n], pw[PW_DARK_T0], pw[PW_DARK_EA])
        for data_level in range(2):
            drop_power_w = p1_w[n] if data_level == 0 else p0_w[n]
            signal_current_a = pw[PW_GAIN_SCALE] * pr[n, PR_RESP] * (drop_power_w + pr[n, PR_BG] * p_bg_w[n])
            mean_code = (
                signal_current_a + photodiode_dark_current_a - pr[n, PR_IBASE]
            ) * codes_per_ampere + pr[n, PR_OFFSET]
            total_noise_psd_a2_per_hz = tia_noise_psd_a2_per_hz + (
                2.0 * Q_E * (abs(signal_current_a) + photodiode_dark_current_a) if shot_on else 0.0
            )
            if rin_per_hz > 0.0:
                line_photocurrent_a = pw[PW_GAIN_SCALE] * pr[n, PR_RESP] * drop_power_w
                total_noise_psd_a2_per_hz += line_photocurrent_a * line_photocurrent_a * rin_per_hz
            code_noise_sigma = (
                math.sqrt(total_noise_psd_a2_per_hz / (4.0 * tau_s)) * abs(codes_per_ampere)
                if tau_s > 0.0
                else 0.0
            )
            if data_level == 0:
                out_mu1[n] = mean_code
                out_sig1[n] = code_noise_sigma
            else:
                out_mu0[n] = mean_code
                out_sig0[n] = code_noise_sigma

code_max[s].
noise - white, temp_sensors[].noise_rms_k per sample (one normal per sample - exact, dt-invariant) - flicker - OU set (fl_coef (S, J, N_FLICKER_COEF)).
tp (S, NTP) - period (S,) and lat (S,) in ticks - code_max (S,).

@njit(cache=True, _nrt=False, inline="always")
def temp_tick_row(k, t_site_k, tp, period, lat, code_max, fl_coef, key, st, fx, fc, primed, fv, fr, fm,
                  out_sampled):
    n_s = t_site_k.shape[0]
    for i in range(n_s):
        out_sampled[i] = 0
        if primed[i] == 0:
            st[i, 0] = 0.0
            st[i, 1] = 0.0
            if fl_coef.shape[1] > 0:
                _flicker_init(key, i, k, _SLOT_FL_INIT, fl_coef[i], fx[i], fc[i])
            primed[i] = 1
        st[i, 0] += t_site_k[i]
        st[i, 1] += 1.0
        if (k + 1) % period[i] != 0:
            continue
        s_tick = k + 1
        t_avg = st[i, 0] / st[i, 1]
        st[i, 0] = 0.0
        st[i, 1] = 0.0
        noise = tp[i, _TP_NOISE] * rng.normal(key, i, s_tick, _SLOT_WHITE)
        if fl_coef.shape[1] > 0:
            noise += flicker_step(key, i, s_tick, _SLOT_FLICKER, fl_coef[i], fx[i], fc[i])
        gref = tp[i, _TP_GAIN_REF_K]
        t_meas = gref + (1.0 + tp[i, _TP_GAIN_ERR]) * (t_avg - gref) + tp[i, _TP_OFFSET] + tp[i, _TP_SELF_HEAT] + noise
        c = _round_clip((t_meas - tp[i, _TP_ZERO_K]) / tp[i, _TP_RESOLUTION], code_max[i])
        ok = fifo_push(fv, fr, fm, i, c, s_tick + lat[i])
        out_sampled[i] = 1 if ok else 2

nodes.name: readback_tick_row
nodes.meaning: heater readback kernels
comments: heater readback kernels
Heater V/I readback of one world (ring.heater.readback) - interval [k, k+1), and the samples at tick k + 1 when it is a multiple of `period`.
v_v, i_a (N,) - heater voltage and current of the interval (V, A - HeaterTickOut.v_v / i_a, rms for dac_pwm).
average = 0 - track-and-hold of the last interval (assumed default) - 1 - boxcar mean over the readback period.

the two codes are packed into one FIFO value (v | i << _RB_I_SHIFT).
