def simulate(
    system: ThermalSystem,  # system = system (mixed units) - assembled thermal states, source maps, and observer maps - type ThermalSystem record
    u_samples_w: ArrayLike,  # u_samples_w = P_samples (W) - source powers at sample boundaries - type array-like, shape (T, S) or (T, B, S)
    h_s: float,  # h_s = h (s) - thermal step duration - type float scalar
    *,
    hold: str = "zoh",  # hold = hold (1) - constant zoh or linear foh power interpolation - type str
    x0: ArrayLike | None = None,  # x0 = x_0 (K) - initial thermal lag-state temperature rises - type array-like, shape (B, M), or None
    t_base_k: ArrayLike = 0.0,  # t_base_k = T_base (K) - base temperature of each world - type array-like, scalar or shape (1 or B,)
    src_scale: ArrayLike | None = None,  # src_scale = s_source (1) - optional source residue multipliers - type array-like, shape (S,) or (1 or B, S), or None
) -> (
    Float64Array  # return = T_observer (K) - observer temperatures at every sample boundary - type float64 ndarray, shape (T, B, O)
):
    u = np.asarray(u_samples_w, dtype=np.float64)
    if u.ndim == 2:
        u = u[:, None, :]
    if hold not in ("zoh", "foh"):
        raise ValueError("hold must be 'zoh' or 'foh'")
    if u.ndim != 3 or u.shape[2] != system.n_src:
        raise ValueError(f"u_samples_w must be (n+1, B|1, S={system.n_src}), got {u.shape}")
    B = max(system.batch, u.shape[1])
    if system.batch not in (1, B) or u.shape[1] not in (1, B):
        raise ValueError(f"batch mismatch: system has {system.batch} worlds, u has {u.shape[1]}")
    a, c0, c1 = system.coefficients(h_s)
    x = np.zeros((B, system.n_lags)) if x0 is None else np.array(x0, dtype=np.float64, copy=True)
    base_temp_k = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(t_base_k, np.float64))
    source_scales = np.ones((1, system.n_src)) if src_scale is None else np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(src_scale,
        np.float64))
    out = np.zeros((u.shape[0], B, system.n_obs))
    write_observer_temperatures(x, system.obs_ptr, base_temp_k, out[0])
    for k in range(u.shape[0] - 1):
        u1 = u[k] if hold == "zoh" else u[k + 1]
        advance_thermal_states(x, a, c0, c1, system.lag_src, np.ascontiguousarray(u[k]), np.ascontiguousarray(u1), source_scales)
        write_observer_temperatures(x, system.obs_ptr, base_temp_k, out[k + 1])
    return out

    Int64Array,  # return[0] = o_selected (1) - selected observer indices - type int64 ndarray, shape (O_selected,)
    Int64Array,  # return[1] = s_selected (1) - selected source indices - type int64 ndarray, shape (S_selected,)
    Int64Array,  # return[2] = m_selected (1) - selected lag indices - type int64 ndarray, shape (M_selected,)
    Int64Array,  # return[3] = o_local (1) - local observer index of each selected lag - type int64 ndarray, shape (M_selected,)
    Int64Array,  # return[4] = s_local (1) - local source index of each selected lag - type int64 ndarray, shape (M_selected,)
]:
    selected_observers = np.arange(system.n_obs) if obs is None else np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(obs, np.int64))
    selected_sources = np.arange(system.n_src) if src is None else np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(src, np.int64))
    observer_map = np.full(system.n_obs, -1, np.int64)
    observer_map[selected_observers] = np.arange(selected_observers.size)
    source_map = np.full(system.n_src, -1, np.int64)
    source_map[selected_sources] = np.arange(selected_sources.size)
    local_observer, local_source = observer_map[system.lag_obs], source_map[system.lag_src]
    selected_lags = np.flatnonzero((local_observer >= 0) & (local_source >= 0))
    return (
        selected_observers,
        selected_sources,
        selected_lags,
        local_observer[selected_lags],
        local_source[selected_lags],
    )

def sum_selected_thermal_responses(
    system: ThermalSystem,  # system = system (mixed units) - assembled thermal states, source maps, and observer maps - type ThermalSystem record
    obs: ArrayLike | None,  # obs = observer_indices (1) - selected observers, or all observers when None - type integer scalar, array-like, or None
    src: ArrayLike | None,  # src = source_indices (1) - selected sources, or all sources when None - type integer scalar, array-like, or None
    kernel: Callable[[Float64Array, Float64Array], NumericArray],  # kernel = kernel (response units) - per-lag response function of time constants and thermal residues - type callable returning a numeric ndarray
) -> (
    NumericArray  # return = response (kernel response units) - selected per-lag contributions summed by source and observer - type numeric ndarray, shape (B, O_selected, S_selected, samples)
):
    selected_observers, selected_sources, selected_lags, local_observer, local_source = select_thermal_response_lags(system, obs, src)
    contributions = kernel(system.taus_s[:, selected_lags], system.res_k_per_w[:,
        selected_lags])           # (B, Msel, F)
    out = np.zeros((system.batch, selected_observers.size, selected_sources.size, contributions.shape[-1]),
        dtype=contributions.dtype)
    np.add.at(out, (slice(None), local_observer, local_source, slice(None)), contributions)
    return out

nodes.name: state_space
nodes.meaning: construct continuous state-space matrices for selected thermal sources and observers.
comments: construct continuous state-space matrices for selected thermal sources and observers.
each selected lag obeys tau_m*dx_m/dt=-x_m+r_m*P_source.
A=diag(-1/tau), B[m,s]=r_m/tau_m, C[o,m]=1, and D=0.
the outputs are temperature rises above the base temperature.
nodes.signature: state_space(system: ThermalSystem, b: int=0, obs: ArrayLike | None=None, src: ArrayLike | None=None)

source_ref.code:
def state_space(
    system: ThermalSystem,  # system = system (mixed units) - assembled thermal states, source maps, and observer maps - type ThermalSystem record
    b: int = 0,  # b = b (1) - world index - type int scalar
    obs: ArrayLike | None = None,  # obs = observer_indices (1) - selected observers, or all observers when None - type integer scalar, array-like, or None
    src: ArrayLike | None = None,  # src = source_indices (1) - selected sources, or all sources when None - type integer scalar, array-like, or None
) -> tuple[
    Float64Array,  # return[0] = A (1/s) - continuous thermal state matrix - type float64 ndarray, shape (M_selected, M_selected)
    Float64Array,  # return[1] = B (K/(W*s)) - source-to-state drive matrix - type float64 ndarray, shape (M_selected, S_selected)
    Float64Array,  # return[2] = C (1) - state-to-observer summation matrix - type float64 ndarray, shape (O_selected, M_selected)
    Float64Array,  # return[3] = D (K/W) - zero direct feedthrough matrix - type float64 ndarray, shape (O_selected, S_selected)
]:
    o_sel, s_sel, m, lio, lis = select_thermal_response_lags(system, obs, src)
    tau = system.taus_s[b, m]
    r = system.res_k_per_w[b, m]
    A = np.diag(-1.0 / tau)
    Bm = np.zeros((m.size, s_sel.size))
    Bm[np.arange(m.size), lis] = r / tau
    C = np.zeros((o_sel.size, m.size))
    C[lio, np.arange(m.size)] = 1.0
    return (
        A,
        Bm,
        C,
        np.zeros((o_sel.size, s_sel.size)),
    )

nodes.meaning: bound the optical feedback gain introduced by using previous-step cross-ring absorbed power.
comments: bound the optical feedback gain introduced by using previous-step cross-ring absorbed power.
g_i sums |c_start+c_end|*max|dP_abs,j/dT_j| over cross-ring lags into ring i.

source_ref.code:
def cross_optical_lag_gain(
    system: ThermalSystem,  # system = system (mixed units) - assembled thermal states, source maps, and observer maps - type ThermalSystem record
    h_s: float,  # h_s = h (s) - thermal step duration - type float scalar
    dpabs_dt_max_w_per_k: ArrayLike,  # dpabs_dt_max_w_per_k = B_dP_dT (W/K) - bounds on absorbed-power temperature derivatives - type array-like, shape (N,) or (B, N)
) -> (
    Float64Array  # return = g_cross (1) - lagged cross-ring optical feedback gain - type float64 ndarray, shape (B, N)
):
    power_slope_bounds = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(dpabs_dt_max_w_per_k, np.float64))
    a, c0, c1 = system.coefficients(h_s)
    cross_lags = np.flatnonzero(system.lag_kind == LAG_OPT_CROSS_RING)
    out = np.zeros((max(system.batch, power_slope_bounds.shape[0]), system.n_rings))
    if cross_lags.size == 0:
        return out
    source_rings = system.src_ring[system.lag_src[cross_lags]]
    observer_rings = system.obs_ring[system.lag_obs[cross_lags]]
    gain_contributions = np.abs(c0[:, cross_lags] + c1[:, cross_lags]) * np.broadcast_to(power_slope_bounds,
        (out.shape[0], power_slope_bounds.shape[1]))[:, source_rings]
    np.add.at(out, (slice(None), observer_rings), gain_contributions)
    return out

nodes.meaning: raise ValueError if the lagged cross-ring optical gain reaches `limit` (default 0.05).
comments: raise ValueError if the lagged cross-ring optical gain reaches `limit` (default 0.05).
returns its max.
nodes.signature: assert_cross_lag_gain(system: ThermalSystem, h_s: float, dpabs_dt_max_w_per_k: ArrayLike, limit: float=0.05)

source_ref.code:
def assert_cross_lag_gain(
    system: ThermalSystem,  # system = system (mixed units) - assembled thermal states, source maps, and observer maps - type ThermalSystem record
    h_s: float,  # h_s = h (s) - thermal step duration - type float scalar
    dpabs_dt_max_w_per_k: ArrayLike,  # dpabs_dt_max_w_per_k = B_dP_dT (W/K) - bounds on absorbed-power temperature derivatives - type array-like, shape (N,) or (B, N)
    limit: float = 0.05,  # limit = g_max (1) - maximum accepted lagged cross-ring optical gain - type float scalar
) -> (
    float  # return = g_cross_max (1) - largest cross-ring optical feedback gain below the limit - type float scalar
):
    g = cross_optical_lag_gain(system, h_s, dpabs_dt_max_w_per_k)
    gmax = float(np.max(g)) if g.size else 0.0
    if gmax >= limit:
        b, i = np.unravel_index(int(np.argmax(g)), g.shape)
        raise ValueError(f"lagged cross-ring optical heating gain {gmax:.3g} >= {limit} at world {b}, ring {i} for a "
                         f"{h_s:g} s substep; reduce the substep or solve the bank jointly")
    return gmax

nodes.name: calculate_conductivity_residue_scale
nodes.meaning: calculate the thermal-resistance multiplier from temperature-dependent conductivity.
comments: calculate the thermal-resistance multiplier from temperature-dependent conductivity.
sum each material's reference-to-current conductivity ratio using its DC resistance share.
the three shares describe silicon film, oxide, and silicon substrate.
apply the result as a source-residue multiplier at a slowly varying temperature.
nodes.signature: calculate_conductivity_residue_scale(t_k: ArrayLike, *, film_nm: float=160.0, weights: Sequence[float]=(0.15, 0.8, 0.05), t_ref_k: float=300.0)

source_ref.code:
def calculate_conductivity_residue_scale(
    t_k: ArrayLike,  # t_k = T (K) - temperatures for conductivity scaling - type array-like, broadcast input shape
    *,
    film_nm: float = 160.0,  # film_nm = d_film (nm) - silicon-film thickness - type float scalar
    weights: Sequence[float] = (0.15, 0.80, 0.05),  # weights = w (1) - film, oxide, and substrate resistance shares - type sequence of three floats
    t_ref_k: float = 300.0,  # t_ref_k = T_ref (K) - reference temperature for conductivity scaling - type float scalar
) -> (
    RealValue  # return = R(T)/R(T_ref) (1) - conductivity-based thermal-residue multiplier - type real scalar or float64 ndarray, shape input temperature shape
):
    from mrm import materials   # Python-level only (never inside a kernel)
    t = np.asarray(t_k, dtype=np.float64)
    w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.float64)
    if w.shape != (3,) or np.any(w < 0) or abs(w.sum() - 1.0) > 1e-9:
        raise ValueError("weights must be three non-negative shares (film, oxide, substrate) summing to 1")
    film_conductivity_ratio = np.asarray(materials.k_si_film_w_per_m_k(t,
        film_nm)) / float(materials.k_si_film_w_per_m_k(t_ref_k, film_nm))
    oxide_conductivity_ratio = np.asarray(materials.k_sio2_w_per_m_k(t)) / float(materials.k_sio2_w_per_m_k(t_ref_k))
    substrate_conductivity_ratio = (np.asarray(materials.k_si_bulk_w_per_m_k(t))
                                    / float(materials.k_si_bulk_w_per_m_k(t_ref_k)))
    return w[0] / film_conductivity_ratio + w[1] / oxide_conductivity_ratio + w[2] / substrate_conductivity_ratio

returns: w[0] / film_conductivity_ratio + w[1] / oxide_conductivity_ratio + w[2] / substrate_conductivity_ratio

nodes.meaning: return the integral of the step response in K s/W, zero before time zero.
comments: return the integral of the step response in K s/W, zero before time zero.

source_ref.code:
def ramp(self, t_s) -> np.ndarray:
        time_s = np.clip(np.asarray(t_s, dtype=np.float64), 0.0, None)[..., None]
        y = time_s / self.taus_s
        series = time_s * y * (0.5 - y / 6.0 + y * y / 24.0)
        exact = time_s + self.taus_s * np.expm1(-y)
        integrated_response = np.sum(self.res_k_per_w * np.where(y < 1e-3, series, exact), axis=-1)
        return integrated_response

def foster_from_system(system, *, victim_ring: int, site: str, observer: str = "ring_mode_weighted",
                       min_abs_res_k_per_w: float = 0.0) -> list[FosterResponse]:
    observer_index = system.observer_index(observer, ring=victim_ring)
    source_index = system.source_index("aggressor", name=site)
    path_indices = np.flatnonzero((np.asarray(system.lag_obs) == observer_index) & (np.asarray(system.lag_src) == source_index))
    if path_indices.size == 0:
        raise ValueError(f"no thermal path from aggressor {site!r} to {observer} of ring {victim_ring}")
    taus = np.asarray(system.taus_s)[:, path_indices]
    residues = np.asarray(system.res_k_per_w)[:, path_indices]
    out = []
    for b in range(taus.shape[0]):
        keep = np.abs(residues[b]) > min_abs_res_k_per_w
        out.append(FosterResponse(taus[b, keep], residues[b, keep],
                                  info={"source": f"thermal system: aggressor {site} -> {observer}[{victim_ring}]",
                                        "world": b}))
    return out

nodes.name: resonance_to_rise_k
nodes.meaning: target
comments: target
invert the temperature law to turn a wavelength shift in m into a rise in K.
start at `t_base_k`.
sensitivity is `s0 * (1 + beta*(T - T_ref))`.
its integral gives `shift = b*x + a*x*x` for rise x, with `a = s0*beta/2` and `b = s0*(1 + beta*(T_base - T_ref))`.
use `2*shift / (b + sqrt(b*b + 4*a*shift))` to avoid cancellation.
reject an unreachable shift or nonpositive starting sensitivity.
when the reference temperature is omitted, use the starting temperature.

nodes.name: _ramp_grid
nodes.meaning: integrate a callable step response on a uniform time grid.
comments: integrate a callable step response on a uniform time grid.
return `R(m*delta)` in K s/W from zero through m_max.
use eight-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature on each interval.
subdivide the first interval geometrically near zero to capture thermal poles faster than the grid.

source_ref.code:
def _ramp_grid(step: Callable, delta: float, m_max: int) -> np.ndarray:
    nodes, weights = _gauss_legendre_01(8)
    interval_starts_s = np.arange(m_max, dtype=np.float64)[:, None] * delta
    sample_times_s = interval_starts_s + nodes[None, :] * delta
    step_values = np.asarray(step(sample_times_s.ravel()), dtype=np.float64).reshape(sample_times_s.shape)
    interval_integrals = delta * (step_values @ weights)
    # refine the first interval toward zero with geometric subintervals.
    edges = delta * np.concatenate([[0.0], 2.0 ** -np.arange(40, -1, -1)])
    first = 0.0
    for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
        graded_times_s = lo + nodes * (hi - lo)
        first += (hi - lo) * float(np.asarray(step(graded_times_s), dtype=np.float64) @ weights)
    if m_max > 0:
        interval_integrals[0] = first
    return np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(interval_integrals)])

nodes.name: _foster_hat_response
nodes.meaning: return the thermal response to one triangular power basis function in K/W.
comments: return the thermal response to one triangular power basis function in K/W.
x is time from the knot center and D is knot spacing in seconds.
the response is `(R(x+D) - 2*R(x) + R(x-D)) / D`.
after the triangle ends, use a closed-form exponential tail to avoid subtracting large ramp responses.

source_ref.code:
def _foster_hat_response(resp: FosterResponse, x: np.ndarray, D: float) -> np.ndarray:
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    tau = resp.taus_s
    r = resp.res_k_per_w
    out = np.zeros_like(x)
    after_hat = x >= D
    if np.any(after_hat):
        tail_times_s = x[after_hat][:, None]
        q = -np.expm1(-D / tau)                                   # 1 - exp(-D/tau)
        out[after_hat] = np.sum(r * tau * np.exp(-(tail_times_s - D) / tau) * q * q, axis=1) / D
    during_hat = ~after_hat
    if np.any(during_hat):
        active_times_s = x[during_hat]
        out[during_hat] = (resp.ramp(active_times_s + D) - 2.0 * resp.ramp(active_times_s) + resp.ramp(active_times_s - D)) / D
    return out

nodes.name: periodic_response_matrix
nodes.meaning: map periodic knot powers in W to steady-state temperature rise in K.
comments: map periodic knot powers in W to steady-state temperature rise in K.
return matrix A and response-truncation metadata.
a has one column per knot and `n_knots*oversample` rows at the fit times.
every column is a shifted response to a triangular basis function.
Foster poles sum all previous periods as an exact geometric series.
a callable response uses numerical ramp integration and a finite history based on its settling time.

def periodic_response_matrix(resp, period_s: float, n_knots: int, oversample: int = 4, *,
                             settle_s: float | None = None) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict]:
    resp = _as_response(resp)
    knot_count = int(n_knots)
    samples_per_knot = int(oversample)                                       # collocation points per knot
    period = float(period_s)
    knot_spacing_s = period / knot_count                                                     # knot spacing, s
    sample_count = knot_count * samples_per_knot                                                 # collocation points per period
    phase_times_s = np.arange(sample_count) * (knot_spacing_s / samples_per_knot)                                # grid of (s - t_j) mod P
    info: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if isinstance(resp, FosterResponse):
        tau = resp.taus_s
        r = resp.res_k_per_w
        q = -np.expm1(-knot_spacing_s / tau)
        # sum the response tails of all earlier periods as a geometric series.
        past_sum = np.sum(r * tau * q * q * np.exp(-(phase_times_s[:,
            None] + period - knot_spacing_s) / tau) / (-np.expm1(-period / tau)),
                          axis=1) / knot_spacing_s
        hat_response = _foster_hat_response(resp, phase_times_s, knot_spacing_s) + past_sum
        wrap = phase_times_s > period - knot_spacing_s                                          # the next period's hat has already started
        hat_response[wrap] += resp.ramp(phase_times_s[wrap] - period + knot_spacing_s) / knot_spacing_s
        info["truncation"] = "exact (closed-form geometric sum)"
    else:
        step = resp
        if settle_s is None:
            settle_s = _estimate_settle_time(step, period)
        past_periods = int(math.ceil(settle_s / period)) + 1                      # number of past periods to sum
        if past_periods > 5000:
            warnings.warn(f"response settles after {settle_s:.3g} s = {past_periods} periods; truncated at 5000",
                          RuntimeWarning, stacklevel=2)
            past_periods = 5000
        ramp_tab = _ramp_grid(step, knot_spacing_s / samples_per_knot,
            (past_periods + 2) * sample_count + 2 * samples_per_knot)   # one extra period for the tail estimate

        def R(idx):                                               # ramp response at grid index idx (0 for idx <= 0)
            idx = np.asarray(idx)
            return np.where(idx > 0, ramp_tab[np.clip(idx, 0, ramp_tab.size - 1)], 0.0)
        grid = np.arange(sample_count)
        hat_response = np.zeros(sample_count)
        for p in range(past_periods + 1):
            k = grid + p * sample_count
            hat_response += (R(k + samples_per_knot) - 2.0 * R(k) + R(k - samples_per_knot)) / knot_spacing_s
        wrap = grid > sample_count - samples_per_knot
        k = grid[wrap] - sample_count + samples_per_knot
        hat_response[wrap] += R(k) / knot_spacing_s
        tail = (R(grid + (past_periods + 1) * sample_count + samples_per_knot)
                - 2 * R(grid + (past_periods + 1) * sample_count)
                + R(grid + (past_periods + 1) * sample_count - samples_per_knot)) / knot_spacing_s
        info["truncation"] = f"{past_periods + 1} periods (settle {settle_s:.3g} s); last term max {np.max(np.abs(tail)):.3g} K/W"
    # each knot contributes the same periodic response shifted to its knot time.
    rows = np.arange(sample_count)[:, None]
    cols = np.arange(knot_count)[None, :]
    response_matrix = hat_response[(rows - cols * samples_per_knot) % sample_count]
    return response_matrix, info

def transient_response_matrix(resp, horizon_s: float, n_knots: int, oversample: int = 4) -> np.ndarray:
    resp = _as_response(resp)
    knot_count = int(n_knots)
    samples_per_knot = int(oversample)                                       # collocation points per knot
    knot_spacing_s = float(horizon_s) / knot_count                                      # knot spacing, s
    sample_count = knot_count * samples_per_knot
    lag = np.arange(-knot_count * samples_per_knot,
        sample_count + 1)                            # (i - j*n_sub) in grid steps
    if isinstance(resp, FosterResponse):
        hat_response = _foster_hat_response(resp, lag * (knot_spacing_s / samples_per_knot), knot_spacing_s)
    else:
        ramp_tab = _ramp_grid(resp, knot_spacing_s / samples_per_knot, sample_count + 2 * samples_per_knot)
        k = lag
        def R(idx):                                               # ramp response at grid index idx (0 for idx <= 0)
            return np.where(idx > 0, ramp_tab[np.clip(idx, 0, ramp_tab.size - 1)], 0.0)
        hat_response = (R(k + samples_per_knot) - 2.0 * R(k) + R(k - samples_per_knot)) / knot_spacing_s
    rows = np.arange(1, sample_count + 1)[:, None]
    cols = np.arange(1, knot_count + 1)[None, :]
    return hat_response[rows - cols * samples_per_knot + knot_count * samples_per_knot]

def calibrate_aggressor_power(response, target: AggressorTarget, *, s0_m_per_k=None, beta_per_k=0.0,
                              t_ref_k=None, ring_t0_k=None, n_knots: int = 256, oversample: int = 4,
                              reg: float = 1e-4, reg_order: int = 1, p_max_w: float | None = None,
                              fit_offset: bool = False, settle_s: float | None = None,
                              response_info: Sequence[Mapping] | Mapping | None = None) -> CalibratedWaveform:
    responses = list(response) if isinstance(response, (list, tuple)) else [response]
    responses = [_as_response(r) for r in responses]
    n_worlds = len(responses)
    if response_info is None:
        response_records = tuple(r.describe() if isinstance(r, FosterResponse) else {"form": "callable step response",
                                                                          "repr": repr(r)} for r in responses)
    else:
        response_records = (tuple(response_info) if not isinstance(response_info, Mapping)
                 else (dict(response_info),) * n_worlds)
    # knots (power) and collocation times (where the fit is checked), s
    periodic = target.period_s is not None
    knot_count = int(n_knots)
    samples_per_knot = int(oversample)                                       # collocation points per knot
    if knot_count < 4 or samples_per_knot < 1:
        raise ValueError("n_knots must be >= 4 and oversample >= 1")
    if periodic:                                                  # knots at 0, D, ..., (n-1) D over one period
        period_s = float(target.period_s)
        knot_spacing_s = period_s / knot_count
        fit_times_s = np.arange(knot_count * samples_per_knot) * (knot_spacing_s / samples_per_knot)
        knot_times_s = np.arange(knot_count) * knot_spacing_s
    else:                                                         # knots at D, ..., n D - the power is 0 at t = 0
        horizon = float(target.horizon_s)
        knot_spacing_s = horizon / knot_count
        fit_times_s = np.arange(1, knot_count * samples_per_knot + 1) * (knot_spacing_s / samples_per_knot)
        knot_times_s = np.arange(1, knot_count + 1) * knot_spacing_s
    # the model's dlambda/dT and the ring temperature with the aggressor off, one value per world
    s0 = None if s0_m_per_k is None else _per_world(s0_m_per_k, n_worlds, "s0_m_per_k")
    beta = _per_world(beta_per_k, n_worlds, "beta_per_k")
    reference_k = None if t_ref_k is None else _per_world(t_ref_k, n_worlds, "t_ref_k")
    starting_temp_k = _per_world(target.t_base_k if ring_t0_k is None else ring_t0_k, n_worlds, "ring_t0_k")
    if target.units == "resonance" and s0 is None:
        raise ValueError("a resonance target needs the model's s0_m_per_k (its dlambda/dT is applied once, to the "
                         "target)")
    diff_op = _difference_operator(knot_count, int(reg_order), periodic)
    # outputs, one row or value per world
    powers = np.zeros((n_worlds, knot_count))
    res_rms = np.zeros(n_worlds)
    res_max = np.zeros(n_worlds)
    target_rms = np.zeros(n_worlds)
    res_rms_m = np.zeros(n_worlds) if target.units == "resonance" else None
    res_max_m = np.zeros(n_worlds) if target.units == "resonance" else None
    offsets = np.zeros(n_worlds) if fit_offset else None
    zero_power_fraction = np.zeros(n_worlds)
    cache: dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}                             # response matrix per distinct response object
    for b, resp in enumerate(responses):
        key = id(resp)
        if key not in cache:
            if periodic:
                response_matrix, _info = periodic_response_matrix(resp, period_s, knot_count, samples_per_knot,
                    settle_s=settle_s)
            else:
                response_matrix = transient_response_matrix(resp, horizon, knot_count, samples_per_knot)
            cache[key] = response_matrix
        response_matrix = cache[key]
        target_rise = target.ring_rise_k(fit_times_s, s0_m_per_k=None if s0 is None else s0[b],
                                         beta_per_k=float(beta[b]),
                                             t_ref_k=None if reference_k is None else float(reference_k[b]),
                                         ring_t0_k=float(starting_temp_k[b]))                       # K at t_coll
        # Tikhonov-regularized least squares with bounds 0 <= p <= p_max (an optional offset column is unbounded)
        regularization_scale = float(reg) * float(np.linalg.norm(response_matrix, 2))
        fit_matrix = response_matrix
        penalty_matrix = diff_op
        lower_bounds = np.zeros(knot_count)
        upper_bounds = np.full(knot_count, np.inf if p_max_w is None else float(p_max_w))
        if fit_offset:
            fit_matrix = np.hstack([response_matrix, np.ones((response_matrix.shape[0], 1))])
            penalty_matrix = np.hstack([diff_op, np.zeros((diff_op.shape[0], 1))])
            lower_bounds = np.append(lower_bounds, -np.inf)
            upper_bounds = np.append(upper_bounds, np.inf)
        lsq_matrix = np.vstack([fit_matrix, regularization_scale * penalty_matrix])
        target_vector = np.concatenate([target_rise, np.zeros(penalty_matrix.shape[0])])
        solution = lsq_linear(lsq_matrix, target_vector, bounds=(lower_bounds, upper_bounds), method="bvls",
            lsq_solver="exact", max_iter=50 * knot_count)
        if not solution.success:
            warnings.warn(f"aggressor calibration, world {b}: BVLS stopped before convergence ({solution.message}); "
                          f"the residual reported below is that of the unconverged power", RuntimeWarning,
                          stacklevel=2)
        # measure physical fit errors without including the smoothness penalty.
        solution_values = solution.x
        power = np.clip(solution_values[:knot_count], 0.0, None)
        powers[b] = power
        fitted_rise_k = response_matrix @ power + (solution_values[knot_count] if fit_offset else 0.0)
        residual_k = fitted_rise_k - target_rise
        res_rms[b] = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(residual_k ** 2)))
        res_max[b] = float(np.max(np.abs(residual_k)))
        target_rms[b] = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(target_rise ** 2)))
        zero_power_fraction[b] = float(np.mean(power <= 1e-12 * max(float(np.max(power)), 1e-300)))
        if fit_offset:
            offsets[b] = float(solution_values[knot_count])
        if target.units == "resonance":
            fitted_shift_m = rise_to_resonance_m(fitted_rise_k, s0_m_per_k=s0[b], beta_per_k=float(beta[b]),
                                      t_ref_k=None if reference_k is None else float(reference_k[b]),
                                          t_base_k=float(starting_temp_k[b]))
            target_shift_m = target.resonance_m(fit_times_s)
            res_rms_m[b] = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((fitted_shift_m - target_shift_m) ** 2)))
            res_max_m[b] = float(np.max(np.abs(fitted_shift_m - target_shift_m)))
    model = {"s0_m_per_k": None if s0 is None else s0.tolist(), "beta_per_k": beta.tolist(),
             "t_ref_k": None if reference_k is None else reference_k.tolist(), "ring_t0_k": starting_temp_k.tolist(),
             "dlambda_dt_applied": "once, in the target (resonance referencing)" if target.units == "resonance"
             else "not applied to the target (temperature referencing)"}
    return CalibratedWaveform(t_knots_s=knot_times_s, power_w=powers, period_s=target.period_s,
                              residual_rms_k=res_rms, residual_max_k=res_max, target_rms_k=target_rms,
                              residual_rms_m=res_rms_m, residual_max_m=res_max_m, offset_k=offsets,
                              lower_bound_fraction=zero_power_fraction, units=target.units, reg=float(reg),
                              reg_order=int(reg_order), oversample=samples_per_knot, response_info=response_records,
                              target_info=target.describe(), model_info=model)

returns: CalibratedWaveform(t_knots_s=knot_times_s, power_w=powers, period_s=target.period_s, residual_rms_k=res_rms, residual_max_k=res_max, target_rms_k=target_rms, residual_rms_m=res_rms_m, residual_max_m=res_max_m, offset_k=offsets, lower_bound_fraction=zero_power_fraction, units=target.units, reg=float(reg), reg_order=int(reg_order), oversample=samples_per_knot, response_info=response_records, target_info=target.describe(), model_info=model)

def calibrate_scenario(scenario: "generators.Scenario", responses: Mapping[str, Any], *,
                       model: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
                       **kw) -> tuple["generators.Scenario", dict[str, CalibratedWaveform]]:
    model = dict(model or {})
    per_site = bool(model) and all(isinstance(v, Mapping) for v in model.values())
    out = {}
    calibrated_scenario = scenario
    for aggressor in scenario.aggressors:
        if not aggressor.pending:
            continue
        if aggressor.site not in responses:
            raise generators.ScenarioError(f"no thermal response given for aggressor site {aggressor.site!r}")
        if per_site and aggressor.site not in model:
            raise generators.ScenarioError(f"model is given per site but has no entry for aggressor site {aggressor.site!r}")
        site_model = dict(model[aggressor.site]) if per_site else model
        waveform = calibrate_aggressor_power(responses[aggressor.site], aggressor.target, **site_model, **kw)
        if waveform.offset_k is not None and np.any(waveform.offset_k != 0.0):
            warnings.warn(f"aggressor {aggressor.site!r}: fitted offset {np.array2string(waveform.offset_k,
                precision=3)} K is not "
                          f"applied to the scenario; move the base temperature by it if it is meant", RuntimeWarning,
                          stacklevel=2)
        if waveform.period_s is not None:
            calibrated_scenario = calibrated_scenario.with_aggressor_power(aggressor.site, waveform.t_knots_s,
                waveform.power_w, period_s=waveform.period_s, record=waveform.record())
        else:
            # prepend the zero initial power before the first one-shot knot.
            t_knots = np.concatenate([[0.0], waveform.t_knots_s])
            power_w = np.concatenate([np.zeros((waveform.power_w.shape[0], 1)), waveform.power_w], axis=1)
            calibrated_scenario = calibrated_scenario.with_aggressor_power(aggressor.site, t_knots, power_w,
                period_s=None, record=waveform.record())
        out[aggressor.site] = waveform
    return calibrated_scenario, out

nodes.name: simulate_foster_foh
nodes.meaning: independent check - exact first-order-hold simulation of a Foster response
comments: independent check - exact first-order-hold simulation of a Foster response
check knot-power response independently using exact first-order hold per pole.
`u_w` contains power samples in W separated by h_s seconds.
interpolate power linearly between samples.
start pole states at x0, or zero.
return the summed temperature rise at each sample and the final pole states.
nodes.signature: simulate_foster_foh(resp: FosterResponse, u_w: np.ndarray, h_s: float, x0=None)

source_ref.code:
def simulate_foster_foh(resp: FosterResponse, u_w: np.ndarray, h_s: float, x0=None) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:

    tau = resp.taus_s
    r = resp.res_k_per_w
    y = h_s / tau
    a = np.exp(-y)
    one_minus_decay = -np.expm1(-y)
    b1 = 1.0 - one_minus_decay / y
    b0 = one_minus_decay / y - a
    x = np.zeros_like(tau) if x0 is None else np.array(x0, dtype=np.float64)
    power_w = np.asarray(u_w, dtype=np.float64)
    rise_k = np.zeros(power_w.size)
    rise_k[0] = x.sum()
    for k in range(power_w.size - 1):
        x = a * x + r * (b0 * power_w[k] + b1 * power_w[k + 1])
        rise_k[k + 1] = x.sum()
    return rise_k, x

nodes.name: _random_walk_value
nodes.meaning: evaluate a random walk at x ticks, with linear interpolation between knots.
comments: evaluate a random walk at x ticks, with linear interpolation between knots.
knot is the knot spacing in ticks.
W_0 = 0 and W_{j+1} = W_j + mu + sd z_j.
mu and sd are the mean and standard
deviation of one increment, in raw-value units.
z_j is a standard normal draw at counter (j, rng_elem, slot).
cache[cache_off:cache_off+3] holds the last (j, W_j, W_{j+1}).
it saves work without changing the result for a different evaluation order.
nodes.signature: _random_walk_value(x, knot, sd, mu, key, rng_elem, slot, cache, cache_off)

source_ref.code:
@njit(cache=True, inline="always")
def _random_walk_value(x, knot, sd, mu, key, rng_elem, slot, cache, cache_off):
    if not (x > 0.0):
        return 0.0
    u = x / knot
    jf = math.floor(u)
    f = u - jf                                               # fraction of the way from knot j to knot j+1
    j = np.int64(jf)
    cached_j = cache[cache_off]
    if cached_j >= 0.0 and np.int64(cached_j) <= j:          # continue from the cached knot
        k0 = np.int64(cached_j)
        v0 = cache[cache_off + 1]
        v1 = cache[cache_off + 2]
    else:                                                    # start again from W_0 = 0
        k0 = np.int64(0)
        v0 = 0.0
        v1 = mu + sd * rng.normal(key, rng_elem, np.int64(0), slot)
    while k0 < j:
        k0 += 1
        v0 = v1
        v1 = v0 + mu + sd * rng.normal(key, rng_elem, k0, slot)
    cache[cache_off] = float(k0)
    cache[cache_off + 1] = v0
    cache[cache_off + 2] = v1
    return v0 + f * (v1 - v0)

nodes.name: _component_value
nodes.meaning: add offset + amp * map(raw(x)) to element e at plant tick t, in signal units.
comments: add offset + amp * map(raw(x)) to element e at plant tick t, in signal units.
x = t_axis - t0 + phase, in ticks.
slow components use t_axis = t * compression.
other components use t_axis = t.
outside [t0, t1), add 0 unless a hold flag applies.
a burst envelope can also set the contribution to 0.
nodes.signature: _component_value(c, t, compression, e, comp_i64, comp_f64_b, tab_b, keys_b, cache_b)

source_ref.code:
@njit(cache=True, inline="always")
def _component_value(c, t, compression, e, comp_i64, comp_f64_b, tab_b, keys_b, cache_b):
    flags = comp_i64[c, CI_FLAGS]
    t_axis = t * compression if (flags & FL_SLOW) != 0 else t     # the component's own time axis, ticks
    t0 = comp_f64_b[c, CF_T0]
    t1 = comp_f64_b[c, CF_T1]
    if t_axis < t0:
        if (flags & FL_HOLD_BEFORE) == 0:
            return 0.0
        t_axis = t0
    elif t_axis >= t1:
        if (flags & FL_HOLD_AFTER) == 0:
            return 0.0
        t_axis = t1 - (1e-9 + 1e-15 * abs(t1))                   # left limit at the window end
    on = comp_f64_b[c, CF_BURST_ON]
    if on > 0.0:                                                  # burst envelope - on for `on`, off for CF_BURST_OFF
        burst_pos = _mod_positive(t_axis - t0 - comp_f64_b[c, CF_BURST_PHASE], on + comp_f64_b[c, CF_BURST_OFF])
        if burst_pos >= on:
            return 0.0
    x = t_axis - t0 + comp_f64_b[c, CF_PHASE]
    kind = comp_i64[c, CI_KIND]
    e_lo = comp_i64[c, CI_E_LO]
    common = (flags & FL_COMMON) != 0
    rng_elem = np.int64(0) if common else np.int64(e)             # element index in the RNG counter
    cache_off = comp_i64[c, CI_CACHE_OFF]
    if kind == K_RANDOM_WALK and not common:                      # one cache entry per element
        cache_off += 3 * (e - e_lo)
    elif kind == K_RANDOM_LEVELS and not common:
        cache_off += 2 * (e - e_lo)
    raw = _raw_value(kind, x, comp_f64_b[c, CF_PERIOD], comp_f64_b[c, CF_P0], comp_f64_b[c, CF_P1],
                     comp_f64_b[c, CF_P2], comp_f64_b[c, CF_P3], comp_f64_b[c, CF_P4], flags, comp_i64[c, CI_DIST],
                     tab_b, comp_i64[c, CI_TAB_OFF], comp_i64[c, CI_TAB_LEN], e - e_lo, keys_b[c], rng_elem,
                     comp_i64[c, CI_SLOT], cache_b, cache_off)
    if comp_i64[c, CI_MAP] == MAP_BERNOULLI_TD:
        raw = 2.0 * raw * (1.0 - raw)
    return comp_f64_b[c, CF_OFFSET] + comp_f64_b[c, CF_AMP] * raw

source_ref.code:
@njit(cache=True, inline="always")
def scen_eval_signal_b(sig, tick, compression, sig_i64, sig_f64, elem_default, comp_i64, comp_f64_b, tab_b, keys_b,
                       cache_b, out):
    t = float(tick)
    off = sig_i64[sig, SI_OFF]
    w = sig_i64[sig, SI_WIDTH]
    for e in range(w):                                            # start from the defaults
        out[off + e] = elem_default[off + e]
    c0 = sig_i64[sig, SI_C0]
    for c in range(c0, c0 + sig_i64[sig, SI_NC]):                 # add every component of the signal
        e_lo = comp_i64[c, CI_E_LO]
        e_hi = comp_i64[c, CI_E_HI]
        if _is_per_element(comp_i64[c, CI_KIND], comp_i64[c, CI_FLAGS]):
            for e in range(e_lo, e_hi):
                out[off + e] += _component_value(c, t, compression, e, comp_i64, comp_f64_b, tab_b, keys_b, cache_b)
        else:
            v = _component_value(c, t, compression, e_lo, comp_i64, comp_f64_b, tab_b, keys_b, cache_b)
            for e in range(e_lo, e_hi):
                out[off + e] += v
    lo = sig_f64[sig, SF_LO]
    hi = sig_f64[sig, SF_HI]
    for e in range(w):                                            # clip to the signal's limits
        v = out[off + e]
        if v < lo:
            out[off + e] = lo
        elif v > hi:
            out[off + e] = hi

source_ref.code:
@njit(cache=True, inline="always")
def _component_next_break(c, t, compression, comp_i64, comp_f64_b, tab_b):
    flags = comp_i64[c, CI_FLAGS]
    axis_scale = compression if (flags & FL_SLOW) != 0 else 1.0   # ticks of the component's axis per plant tick
    t_axis = t * axis_scale
    t0 = comp_f64_b[c, CF_T0]
    t1 = comp_f64_b[c, CF_T1]
    if t_axis < t0:
        return t0 / axis_scale
    if t_axis >= t1:
        return math.inf
    best = t1
    on = comp_f64_b[c, CF_BURST_ON]
    if on > 0.0:                                                  # the next switch of the burst envelope
        per = on + comp_f64_b[c, CF_BURST_OFF]
        burst_pos = _mod_positive(t_axis - t0 - comp_f64_b[c, CF_BURST_PHASE], per)
        nxt = on - burst_pos if burst_pos < on else per - burst_pos
        best = min(best, t_axis + nxt)
    x = t_axis - t0 + comp_f64_b[c, CF_PHASE]
    dx = _raw_next_break(comp_i64[c, CI_KIND], x, comp_f64_b[c, CF_PERIOD], comp_f64_b[c, CF_P0],
                         comp_f64_b[c, CF_P1], comp_f64_b[c, CF_P2], flags, tab_b, comp_i64[c, CI_TAB_OFF],
                         comp_i64[c, CI_TAB_LEN], comp_f64_b[c, CF_HSMOOTH])
    h_smooth = comp_f64_b[c, CF_HSMOOTH]    # curved components (smooth kinds, mapped ramps) break every h_smooth ticks
    if h_smooth < dx:
        dx = h_smooth
    best = min(best, t_axis + dx)
    return best / axis_scale

nodes.name: np_trapezoid
nodes.meaning: NumPy reference shapes (used by calibrate.py, the library and the tests)
comments: NumPy reference shapes (used by calibrate.py, the library and the tests)
NumPy version of the trapezoid raw value (0 -> 1 -> 0) at local times x (array - all times in the same unit).

source_ref.code:
def np_trapezoid(x, period, rise, high, fall):
    xm = np.mod(np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64), period)
    out = np.zeros_like(xm)
    if rise > 0:
        m = xm < rise
        out[m] = xm[m] / rise
    m = (xm >= rise) & (xm < rise + high)
    out[m] = 1.0
    if fall > 0:
        m = (xm >= rise + high) & (xm < rise + high + fall)
        out[m] = 1.0 - (xm[m] - rise - high) / fall
    return out

def fingerprint(self, *, include_compression: bool = True) -> str:
        d = {
            "name": self.name,
            "components": [c.describe() for c in self.components],
            "aggressors": [{"site": a.site, "victim_ring": a.victim_ring,
                            "target": None if a.target is None else a.target.describe(),
                            "power": [c.describe() for c in a.power]} for a in self.aggressors],
            "defaults": {k: np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float64).tolist() for k, v in sorted(self.defaults.items())},
            "reset": None if self.reset is None else dataclasses.asdict(self.reset),
        }
        if include_compression:
            d["time_compression"] = float(self.time_compression)
        text = json.dumps(d, sort_keys=True, default=str, allow_nan=True)
        return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]

def _to_ticks(v_s: float, dt_s: float) -> float:
    time_s = float(v_s)
    if not math.isfinite(time_s):
        return time_s
    ticks = time_s / dt_s
    nearest_tick = round(ticks)
    return float(nearest_tick) if abs(ticks - nearest_tick) <= _SNAP_TICKS + 1e-12 * abs(ticks) else ticks

source_ref.code:
def _compile_scenario(sc: Scenario, *, dt_s: float, n_rings: int, n_lines: int, batch: int, seed: int,
                      aggressor_sites: Sequence[str] | None, check_compression: bool) -> ScenarioArrays:
    if not (dt_s > 0 and math.isfinite(dt_s)):
        raise ScenarioError(f"dt_s must be a positive finite number, got {dt_s}")
    if n_rings < 1 or n_lines < 1 or batch < 1:
        raise ScenarioError("n_rings, n_lines and batch must be >= 1")
    pend = sc.pending_aggressors
    if pend:
        raise ScenarioError(f"scenario {sc.name!r}: aggressor(s) {list(pend)} have a target but no power waveform; "
                            f"run mrm.scenarios.calibrate.calibrate_scenario with the plant's thermal response "
                            f"first (the power is calibrated so that the victim ring follows the target)")
    sites = tuple(aggressor_sites) if aggressor_sites is not None else sc.aggressor_sites
    for s in sc.aggressor_sites:
        if s not in sites:
            raise ScenarioError(f"aggressor site {s!r} is not among the engine's aggressor sites {list(sites)}")
    widths = {"die": 1, "ring": n_rings, "line": n_lines, "aggressor": len(sites)}

    # signal layout (fixed order of SIGNALS)
    layout: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    off = 0
    for s in SIGNALS:
        w = widths[s.level]
        layout[s.name] = (off, w)
        off += w
    n_out = off

    # defaults
    elem_default = np.zeros(n_out)
    for s in SIGNALS:
        o, w = layout[s.name]
        v = sc.defaults.get(s.name, s.default)
        a = np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float64)
        if a.ndim == 0:
            elem_default[o:o + w] = float(a)
        elif a.shape == (w,):
            elem_default[o:o + w] = a
        else:
            raise ScenarioError(f"default of {s.name} must be a scalar or ({w},), got shape {a.shape}")

    # component entries split into contiguous element runs
    entries: list[tuple[Component, int, int, list[int]]] = []
    idx_of: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
    for c in sc.all_components:
        spec = c.spec
        w = widths[spec.level]
        if c.site is not None:
            idx = [sites.index(c.site)]
        elif c.elements is None:
            idx = list(range(w))
        else:
            idx = [int(e) for e in c.elements]
        if not idx:
            continue
        idx_of[id(c)] = idx
        bad = [e for e in idx if not 0 <= e < w]
        if bad:
            raise ScenarioError(f"{c.label or c.kind} on {c.signal}: elements {bad} out of range 0..{w - 1}")
        for lo, hi, pos in _element_runs(idx):
            entries.append((c, lo, hi, pos))
    entries.sort(key=lambda t: SIGNAL_BY_NAME[t[0].signal].id)

    # absolute components replace element defaults.
    # two absolute components on one element are an error.
    abs_owner: dict[tuple[str, int], Component] = {}
    for c, lo, hi, _ in entries:
        if not c.absolute:
            continue
        o, _w = layout[c.signal]
        for e in range(lo, hi):
            k = (c.signal, e)
            if k in abs_owner and abs_owner[k] is not c:
                raise ScenarioError(f"{c.signal}[{e}] is set absolutely by both {abs_owner[k].label or 'a component'!r}"
                                    f" and {c.label or c.kind!r}; one absolute definition per element")
            abs_owner[k] = c
            elem_default[o + e] = 0.0

    # an additive component would retain a NaN default.
    # require an absolute value or a finite default.
    for c, lo, hi, _ in entries:
        if c.absolute:
            continue
        o, _w = layout[c.signal]
        nan_el = [e for e in range(lo, hi) if math.isnan(elem_default[o + e])]
        if nan_el:
            raise ScenarioError(f"{c.label or c.kind} adds to {c.signal}{nan_el}, whose default is NaN (not driven); "
                                f"make it absolute or set the signal default (e.g. scenario.bias_v)")

    # duplicate random draws on one signal (same stream and slot, different components) are almost always a bug
    seen_slots: dict[tuple[str, str, int], Component] = {}
    for c, _lo, _hi, _ in entries:
        if c.is_random:
            k = (c.signal, c.stream, c.slot)
            if k in seen_slots and seen_slots[k] is not c:
                raise ScenarioError(f"components {seen_slots[k].label or seen_slots[k].kind!r} and "
                                    f"{c.label or c.kind!r} on {c.signal} share stream {c.stream} and slot {c.slot} "
                                    f"(identical draws): give them different labels or links")
            seen_slots[k] = c

    # per-world rows - bs = 1 when every component is shared by all worlds, else B
    world_counts = [c.world_count() for c, *_ in entries]
    for n in world_counts:
        if n not in (1, batch):
            raise ScenarioError(f"per-world arrays have {n} rows but the batch is {batch}")
    bs = batch if any(n == batch for n in world_counts) and batch > 1 else 1

    C = len(entries)                        # number of component entries (one per contiguous element run)
    comp_i64 = np.zeros((C, NCI), dtype=np.int64)
    comp_f64 = np.zeros((bs, C, NCF), dtype=np.float64)
    tables: list[np.ndarray] = []           # each (bs, len)
    tab_off = 0
    cache_off = 0
    sig_i64 = np.zeros((len(SIGNALS), NSI), dtype=np.int64)
    sig_f64 = np.zeros((len(SIGNALS), NSF), dtype=np.float64)
    for s in SIGNALS:
        o, w = layout[s.name]
        sig_i64[s.id, SI_OFF] = o
        sig_i64[s.id, SI_WIDTH] = w
        sig_f64[s.id, SF_LO] = s.lo
        sig_f64[s.id, SF_HI] = s.hi

    def tile(a: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:            # (n_rows, ...) -> (bs, ...)
        return np.broadcast_to(a, (bs,) + a.shape[1:]) if a.shape[0] == 1 else a

    # divide foh_tol among curved components because their errors from a straight line can add.
    n_smooth: dict[str, int] = {}
    for c, *_r in entries:
        if _smooth_curvature(c, 1.0) > 0.0:
            n_smooth[c.signal] = n_smooth.get(c.signal, 0) + 1
    # reachable value range per output element (for SI_CLIP) - default (0 under an absolute component) + components
    v_lo = np.nan_to_num(elem_default.copy(), nan=0.0)
    v_hi = v_lo.copy()

    # one row of comp_i64 / comp_f64 per entry
    for ci, (c, lo, hi, pos) in enumerate(entries):
        spec = c.spec
        sid = spec.id
        if sig_i64[sid, SI_NC] == 0:
            sig_i64[sid, SI_C0] = ci
        sig_i64[sid, SI_NC] += 1
        flags = 0
        flags |= FL_SLOW if c.slow else 0
        flags |= FL_ABSOLUTE if c.absolute else 0
        flags |= FL_COMMON if c.common else 0
        flags |= FL_HOLD_BEFORE if c.hold_before else 0
        flags |= FL_HOLD_AFTER if c.hold_after else 0
        flags |= FL_PERIODIC if c.periodic else 0
        flags |= FL_LINEAR if c.linear else 0
        comp_i64[ci, CI_KIND] = KINDS.index(c.kind)
        comp_i64[ci, CI_SIGNAL] = sid
        comp_i64[ci, CI_E_LO] = lo
        comp_i64[ci, CI_E_HI] = hi
        comp_i64[ci, CI_MAP] = MAPS.index(c.map)
        comp_i64[ci, CI_DIST] = DISTS.index(c.dist)
        comp_i64[ci, CI_SLOT] = c.slot
        # tables (times in ticks, values in signal units), appended side by side to tab_f64
        tab = None
        if c.kind == "pwl":
            tt = np.asarray(c.table_t, dtype=np.float64)
            n = tt.size
            tv = _as_rows_elements(np.asarray(c.table_v, dtype=np.float64))                  # (rows, E, n)
            if tv.shape[-1] != n:
                raise ScenarioError(f"{c.label or 'pwl'}: table_v has {tv.shape[-1]} points, table_t {n}")
            if tv.shape[1] > 1:
                _check_element_rows(c, tv, idx_of[id(c)])
                tv = tv[:, pos, :]
                flags |= FL_PER_ELEMENT
            tv = tile(tv)
            tab = np.concatenate([np.broadcast_to(_to_ticks_array(tt, dt_s), (bs, n)), tv.reshape(bs, -1)], axis=1)
            comp_i64[ci, CI_TAB_LEN] = n
        elif c.kind == "sampled":
            tv = _as_rows_elements(np.asarray(c.table_v, dtype=np.float64))
            n = tv.shape[-1]
            if n < 1:
                raise ScenarioError(f"{c.label or 'sampled'}: empty table")
            if tv.shape[1] > 1:
                _check_element_rows(c, tv, idx_of[id(c)])
                tv = tv[:, pos, :]
                flags |= FL_PER_ELEMENT
            tab = tile(tv).reshape(bs, -1)
            comp_i64[ci, CI_TAB_LEN] = n
        elif c.kind == "random_levels" and c.dist == "choice":
            tv = np.asarray(c.table_v, dtype=np.float64).ravel()
            tab = np.broadcast_to(tv, (bs, tv.size))
            comp_i64[ci, CI_TAB_LEN] = tv.size
        if tab is not None:
            comp_i64[ci, CI_TAB_OFF] = tab_off
            tables.append(np.ascontiguousarray(tab))
            tab_off += tab.shape[1]
        if c.kind == "random_walk":
            comp_i64[ci, CI_CACHE_OFF] = cache_off
            cache_off += 3 * (1 if c.common else hi - lo)
        elif c.kind == "random_levels":
            comp_i64[ci, CI_CACHE_OFF] = cache_off
            cache_off += 2 * (1 if c.common else hi - lo)
        comp_i64[ci, CI_FLAGS] = flags
        # floats (times converted to ticks)
        amp = tile(_world_array(c.amp, "amp")[:, None])[:, 0]
        offset = tile(_world_array(c.offset, "offset")[:, None])[:, 0]
        to_ticks = lambda v: _to_ticks(v, dt_s)              # noqa: E731  seconds -> ticks, snapped to the grid
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_T0] = to_ticks(c.t0_s)
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_T1] = to_ticks(c.t1_s)
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_AMP] = amp
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_OFFSET] = offset
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_PERIOD] = to_ticks(c.period_s)
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_PHASE] = to_ticks(c.phase_s)
        kind_params = list(c.params)
        if c.kind == "trapezoid":
            kind_params[0], kind_params[1], kind_params[2] = (to_ticks(kind_params[0]), to_ticks(kind_params[1]),
                                                              to_ticks(kind_params[2]))
            excess = kind_params[0] + kind_params[1] + kind_params[2] - to_ticks(c.period_s)
            if excess > 0:                                   # snapping pushed the sum past the period
                kind_params[2] = max(0.0, kind_params[2] - excess)
        elif c.kind == "smooth_step":
            kind_params[0] = to_ticks(kind_params[0])
        elif c.kind == "random_walk":
            # (knot in ticks, sd per knot = sigma * sqrt(knot_s), mean step per knot = drift * knot_s)
            knot = to_ticks(kind_params[0])
            kind_params = [knot, kind_params[1] * math.sqrt(knot * dt_s), kind_params[2] * knot * dt_s, 0.0, 0.0]
        elif c.kind in ("random_levels", "sampled"):
            kind_params[0] = to_ticks(kind_params[0])
        for k in range(5):
            comp_f64[:, ci, CF_P0 + k] = kind_params[k]
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_BURST_ON] = to_ticks(c.burst_on_s)
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_BURST_OFF] = to_ticks(c.burst_off_s)
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_BURST_PHASE] = to_ticks(c.burst_phase_s)
        # CF_HSMOOTH limits the error from a straight line.
        # kappa bounds |f''| in signal units per s^2.
        # over h seconds, the error is at most kappa h^2 / 8.
        # use this component's share of foh_tol as tol.
        kappa = _smooth_curvature(c, float(np.max(np.abs(amp))))
        tol = spec.foh_tol / max(1, n_smooth.get(c.signal, 1))
        comp_f64[:, ci, CF_HSMOOTH] = math.sqrt(8.0 * tol / kappa) / dt_s if kappa > 0 else math.inf
        val_lo, val_hi = _component_value_range(c, np.asarray(amp), np.asarray(offset))
        sig_off = layout[c.signal][0]
        v_lo[sig_off + lo:sig_off + hi] += val_lo
        v_hi[sig_off + lo:sig_off + hi] += val_hi
        # aliasing guard - require at least 4 ticks per fast period.
        # this is a design choice.
        if c.kind in ("sine", "rect_sine", "trapezoid") and not c.slow and c.period_s < 4 * dt_s:
            warnings.warn(f"{c.label or c.kind} on {c.signal}: period {c.period_s} s is below 4 plant ticks "
                          f"({dt_s} s); it aliases on the tick grid", RuntimeWarning, stacklevel=3)

    # SI_CLIP marks signals whose reachable range passes a finite clip limit.
    for s in SIGNALS:
        o, w = layout[s.name]
        if w == 0 or sig_i64[s.id, SI_NC] == 0:
            continue
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
            span = max(1.0, float(np.nanmax(np.abs(np.concatenate([v_lo[o:o + w], v_hi[o:o + w]])))))
        eps = 1e-12 * span if math.isfinite(span) else 0.0
        if np.any(v_lo[o:o + w] < s.lo - eps) or np.any(v_hi[o:o + w] > s.hi + eps):
            sig_i64[s.id, SI_CLIP] = 1

    tab_f64 = np.concatenate(tables, axis=1) if tables else np.zeros((bs, 0))
    # counter-RNG keys - one per batch element and component, from the batch seed and the component's stream
    seeds = rng.batch_seeds(seed, batch)
    keys = np.zeros((batch, C), dtype=np.uint64)
    for ci, (c, *_r) in enumerate(entries):
        sid = rng.stream_id(c.stream)
        for b in range(batch):
            keys[b, ci] = rng.stream_key(np.int64(seeds[b]), np.int64(sid))
    cache0 = np.zeros((batch, cache_off), dtype=np.float64)
    for ci, (c, lo, hi, _) in enumerate(entries):
        if c.is_random:
            o = comp_i64[ci, CI_CACHE_OFF]
            w = 3 if c.kind == "random_walk" else 2
            for e in range(1 if c.common else hi - lo):
                cache0[:, o + w * e] = -1.0                  # no cached knot / interval

    rep: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if check_compression:
        rep = check_time_compression(sc)
    return ScenarioArrays(
        sig_i64=sig_i64, sig_f64=sig_f64, elem_default=elem_default, comp_i64=comp_i64,
        comp_f64=np.ascontiguousarray(comp_f64), tab_f64=np.ascontiguousarray(tab_f64), keys=keys, cache0=cache0,
        compression=float(sc.time_compression), dt_s=dt_s, batch=batch, n_rings=n_rings, n_lines=n_lines,
        aggressor_sites=sites, layout=layout, n_out=n_out, drives=sc.drives, offsets=sc.offsets, reset=sc.reset,
        fingerprint=sc.fingerprint(), component_labels=tuple(c.label or c.kind for c, *_ in entries),
        compression_report=rep)

returns: ScenarioArrays(sig_i64=sig_i64, sig_f64=sig_f64, elem_default=elem_default, comp_i64=comp_i64, comp_f64=np.ascontiguousarray(comp_f64), tab_f64=np.ascontiguousarray(tab_f64), keys=keys, cache0=cache0, compression=float(sc.time_compression), dt_s=dt_s, batch=batch, n_rings=n_rings, n_lines=n_lines, aggressor_sites=sites, layout=layout, n_out=n_out, drives=sc.drives, offsets=sc.offsets, reset=sc.reset, fingerprint=sc.fingerprint(), component_labels=tuple((c.label or c.kind for c, *_ in entries)), compression_report=rep)

nodes.meaning: time compression - the rate rule and the convergence experiment
comments: time compression - the rate rule and the convergence experiment
bound the absolute contribution rate on the component's own axis, in signal units per s.
jumps, such as steps and random levels, count as 0 because this rule compares ramp rates.
the random-walk estimate is |drift| + 4 sigma / sqrt(knot_s).

nodes.name: check_time_compression
nodes.meaning: check compressed ramp rates at load time and return a report.
comments: check compressed ramp rates at load time and return a report.
raise CompressionError on a violation.
each slow component must stay at or below fraction times Scenario.fast_rate_ref_k_per_s after time compression.
the default fraction is 1 %.
the default reference is the slide-10 peak of 2127 K/s.
this keeps compressed drifts slow relative to the transients that the control loop must track.
rate_to_k_per_s converts signal rates to K/s equivalents.
laser frequency uses Lightmatter's 15 GHz/degC.
a compressed ramp without an equivalent, such as dB, produces a warning.
the report includes time_compression, limit_k_per_s and a components mapping.
checked entries give rate_k_per_s, limit_k_per_s and max_compression.
unchecked entries give rate_per_s, unit and checked = False.

nodes.name: a1_slide10_aggressor
nodes.meaning: on-die aggressors (path 2 - heater power into the ROM)
comments: on-die aggressors (path 2 - heater power into the ROM)
build the A1 slide-10 rectified-sine aggressor target at the victim ring.
the corrected read-off fit is `113.6 - 88.5*abs(sin(pi*t/0.1307))` degC.
it ranges from 25.1 to 113.6 degC, with peak rate 2127 K/s and mean absolute rate 1354 K/s.
the fit error is 0.34 degC RMS.
the older parabolic reading fits five times worse and would imply a 2780 K/s peak.
CAL-13a checks the fit.
resonance referencing interprets the plotted temperature through the published 15 GHz/K conversion, about 85.86 pm/K at 1310 nm.
temperature referencing uses the ring rise, corrected by `thermometer_fraction` for a remote sensor.
the symmetric-triangle alternative keeps the swing and period.
calibration later finds nonnegative heater power at `site` that produces the target through the thermal model.
this also heats neighboring observers.
the scenario cannot compile before calibration.
`set_base` supplies the assumed aggressor-off temperature as a default.
a stacked base profile replaces it.
nodes.signature: a1_slide10_aggressor(*, site: str='aggressor', victim_ring: int=0, referencing: str='resonance', waveform: str='rectified_sine', t_max_c: float=A1_T_MAX_C, delta_t_k: float=A1_DELTA_T_K, period_s: float=A1_PERIOD_S, t_base_c: float=A1_T_BASE_C, phase_s: float=0.0, thermometer_fraction: float=1.0, dlambda_dt_ref_pm_per_k: float | None=None, set_base: bool=True)

source_ref.code:
def a1_slide10_aggressor(*, site: str = "aggressor", victim_ring: int = 0, referencing: str = "resonance",
                         waveform: str = "rectified_sine", t_max_c: float = A1_T_MAX_C,
                         delta_t_k: float = A1_DELTA_T_K, period_s: float = A1_PERIOD_S,
                         t_base_c: float = A1_T_BASE_C, phase_s: float = 0.0, thermometer_fraction: float = 1.0,
                         dlambda_dt_ref_pm_per_k: float | None = None, set_base: bool = True) -> generators.Scenario:
    if waveform not in ("rectified_sine", "symmetric_triangle"):
        raise generators.ScenarioError(f"A1 waveform must be rectified_sine or symmetric_triangle, got {waveform!r}")
    reference_slope_m_per_k = LM_DLAMBDA_DT_M_PER_K if dlambda_dt_ref_pm_per_k is None else dlambda_dt_ref_pm_per_k * 1e-12
    common = dict(units=referencing, period_s=float(period_s), t_base_k=_c_to_k(t_base_c), delta_k=float(delta_t_k),
                  s_ref_m_per_k=reference_slope_m_per_k, thermometer_fraction=thermometer_fraction,
                      name="A1 slide-10 aggressor",
                  provenance="read-off", source="LM26-S",
                  note="slide 10 temperature panel; rectified-sine fit 0.34 degC rms (01 verification log item 5)")
    if waveform == "rectified_sine":
        target = AggressorTarget(form="rectified_sine", t_max_k=_c_to_k(t_max_c), phase_s=float(phase_s), **common)
    else:
        # start the triangle at its maximum to match the rectified-sine phase.
        target = AggressorTarget(form="trapezoid", t_low_k=_c_to_k(t_max_c - delta_t_k), rise_s=period_s / 2,
            high_s=0.0,
                              fall_s=period_s / 2, phase_s=float(phase_s) + period_s / 2, **common)
    # a base-temperature profile replaces this default when scenarios are stacked.
    # scenario.ambient_c can also override it.
    defaults = {"thermal.t_base_k": _c_to_k(t_base_c)} if set_base else {}
    return generators.Scenario(
        name="a1_slide10_aggressor", defaults=defaults,
        aggressors=(generators.AggressorSpec(site=site, victim_ring=int(victim_ring), target=target,
                                             note="power calibrated so that the victim ring follows the target"),),
        description=f"A1 slide-10 aggressor ({waveform}, {referencing} referencing): {t_max_c} - {delta_t_k} "
                    f"|sin(pi t/{period_s})| degC at ring {victim_ring}",
        provenance=({"item": "A1 trajectory", "value": [t_max_c, delta_t_k, period_s], "provenance": "read-off",
                     "source": "LM26-S", "note": "01 verification log item 5 (rectified sine, corrected)"},
                    {"item": "15 GHz/degC", "value": reference_slope_m_per_k, "provenance": "printed",
                        "source": "LM26-P",
                     "note": "aside in section 1; used only to express printed degC as resonance"},
                    {"item": "A1 base temperature", "value": t_base_c, "provenance": "assumed", "source": "LM26-P",
                     "note": "package at the printed 25 degC lower end during the run (signal default)"}))

returns: generators.Scenario(name='a1_slide10_aggressor', defaults=defaults, aggressors=(generators.AggressorSpec(site=site, victim_ring=int(victim_ring), target=target, note='power calibrated so that the victim ring follows the target'),), description=f'A1 slide-10 aggressor ({waveform}, {referencing} referencing): {t_max_c} - {delta_t_k} |sin(pi t/{period_s})| degC at ring {victim_ring}', provenance=({'item': 'A1 trajectory', 'value': [t_max_c, delta_t_k, period_s], 'provenance': 'read-off', 'source': 'LM26-S', 'note': '01 verification log item 5 (rectified sine, corrected)'}, {'item': '15 GHz/degC', 'value': reference_slope_m_per_k, 'provenance': 'printed', 'source': 'LM26-P', 'note': 'aside in section 1; used only to express printed degC as resonance'}, {'item': 'A1 base temperature', 'value': t_base_c, 'provenance': 'assumed', 'source': 'LM26-P', 'note': 'package at the printed 25 degC lower end during the run (signal default)'}))

nodes.name: a2_808_aggressor
nodes.meaning: build A2 from the paper's stated 808 K/s, temperature range, and period.
comments: build A2 from the paper's stated 808 K/s, temperature range, and period.
the paper does not resolve the waveform.
`reading` selects an interpretation.
the default symmetric triangle takes 808 as swing per 100 ms, giving 80.8 K and edges of 1616 K/s.
the rectified sine keeps that swing and period, with a 2538 K/s peak.
both run from 25 to 105.8 degC with the default values.
the one-sided sawtooth takes 808 K/s as the actual rise slope.
an 80 K rise takes 99 ms, leaving about 1 ms to cool.
calibration exposes the large return error because a heater cannot remove heat that fast.
`ramp_per_period` uses 808 K/s for both ramps, making a 200 ms cycle with an 80.8 K swing.
the thermal notes favor that interpretation from the arithmetic.
these are hypotheses.
apply the same target referencing and power calibration as A1.
CAL-13b checks the stated rate.
the published run may use the same heater as A1.
nodes.signature: a2_808_aggressor(*, site: str='aggressor', victim_ring: int=0, referencing: str='resonance', reading: str='symmetric_triangle', rate_k_per_s: float=A2_RATE_K_PER_S, t_low_c: float=A2_T_LOW_C, t_high_c: float | None=None, period_s: float=A2_PERIOD_S, t_base_c: float | None=None, thermometer_fraction: float=1.0, dlambda_dt_ref_pm_per_k: float | None=None, set_base: bool=True)

source_ref.code:
def a2_808_aggressor(*, site: str = "aggressor", victim_ring: int = 0, referencing: str = "resonance",
                     reading: str = "symmetric_triangle", rate_k_per_s: float = A2_RATE_K_PER_S,
                     t_low_c: float = A2_T_LOW_C, t_high_c: float | None = None, period_s: float = A2_PERIOD_S,
                     t_base_c: float | None = None, thermometer_fraction: float = 1.0,
                     dlambda_dt_ref_pm_per_k: float | None = None, set_base: bool = True) -> generators.Scenario:
    if reading not in ("symmetric_triangle", "rectified_sine", "one_sided_sawtooth", "ramp_per_period"):
        raise generators.ScenarioError(f"unknown A2 reading {reading!r}")
    reference_slope_m_per_k = LM_DLAMBDA_DT_M_PER_K if dlambda_dt_ref_pm_per_k is None else dlambda_dt_ref_pm_per_k * 1e-12
    base_c = t_low_c if t_base_c is None else t_base_c                 # base temperature, degC
    if reading == "one_sided_sawtooth":
        high_c = A2_T_HIGH_C if t_high_c is None else t_high_c
        swing_k = high_c - t_low_c
        rise_s = swing_k / rate_k_per_s
        if rise_s >= period_s:
            raise generators.ScenarioError(f"one-sided sawtooth: a {swing_k} K ramp at {rate_k_per_s} K/s does not fit in "
                                           f"{period_s} s")
        shape = dict(form="trapezoid", t_low_k=_c_to_k(t_low_c), rise_s=rise_s, high_s=0.0, fall_s=period_s - rise_s)
    elif reading == "ramp_per_period":
        swing_k = rate_k_per_s * period_s if t_high_c is None else t_high_c - t_low_c
        ramp_s = swing_k / rate_k_per_s                                  # = period_s for the printed numbers
        shape = dict(form="trapezoid", t_low_k=_c_to_k(t_low_c), rise_s=ramp_s, high_s=0.0, fall_s=ramp_s)
        period_s = 2.0 * ramp_s                                     # the cycle is two ramps
    else:
        swing_k = rate_k_per_s * period_s if t_high_c is None else t_high_c - t_low_c
        if reading == "symmetric_triangle":
            shape = dict(form="trapezoid", t_low_k=_c_to_k(t_low_c), rise_s=period_s / 2, high_s=0.0,
                         fall_s=period_s / 2)
        else:
            shape = dict(form="rectified_sine", t_max_k=_c_to_k(t_low_c + swing_k))
    target = AggressorTarget(units=referencing, period_s=float(period_s), t_base_k=_c_to_k(base_c),
        delta_k=float(swing_k),
                          s_ref_m_per_k=reference_slope_m_per_k, thermometer_fraction=thermometer_fraction,
                          name=f"A2 808 degC/s ({reading})", provenance="printed", source="LM26-P",
                          note="section 3.2; waveform not published, reading is a hypothesis (01 D7)", **shape)
    defaults = {"thermal.t_base_k": _c_to_k(base_c)} if set_base else {}     # a default - stacks with soak / cold start
    return generators.Scenario(
        name="a2_808_aggressor", defaults=defaults,
        aggressors=(generators.AggressorSpec(site=site, victim_ring=int(victim_ring), target=target),),
        description=f"A2 808 degC/s aggressor, reading {reading}, dT {swing_k:.4g} K, period {period_s} s",
        provenance=({"item": "A2", "value": [rate_k_per_s, t_low_c, period_s], "provenance": "printed",
                     "source": "LM26-P", "note": f"reading {reading} (hypothesis)"},))

returns: generators.Scenario(name='a2_808_aggressor', defaults=defaults, aggressors=(generators.AggressorSpec(site=site, victim_ring=int(victim_ring), target=target),), description=f'A2 808 degC/s aggressor, reading {reading}, dT {swing_k:.4g} K, period {period_s} s', provenance=({'item': 'A2', 'value': [rate_k_per_s, t_low_c, period_s], 'provenance': 'printed', 'source': 'LM26-P', 'note': f'reading {reading} (hypothesis)'},))

nodes.meaning: base temperature (path 1) and XPU events (path 3)
comments: base temperature (path 1) and XPU events (path 3)
cycle the package base temperature for the read-off endurance test.
defaults give 90 triangular cycles from 33 to 108 degC, each 20.3 minutes.
the rate is about 0.123 K/s and total duration is 30.45 hours.
hold the final temperature after the last cycle.
these are read-offs of one experiment.
time compression speeds up this slow signal.
the load-time rule keeps its rate below one percent of the fast transient rate, limiting compression to about 170.
report a compressed result only after the one-cycle convergence comparison at factors 1, 10, and 100 passes.
nodes.signature: soak(*, t_low_c: float=SOAK_T_LOW_C, t_high_c: float=SOAK_T_HIGH_C, cycle_s: float=SOAK_CYCLE_S, n_cycles: int=SOAK_N_CYCLES, start: str='low', time_compression: float=1.0, compressible: bool=True)

source_ref.code:
def soak(*, t_low_c: float = SOAK_T_LOW_C, t_high_c: float = SOAK_T_HIGH_C, cycle_s: float = SOAK_CYCLE_S,
         n_cycles: int = SOAK_N_CYCLES, start: str = "low", time_compression: float = 1.0,
         compressible: bool = True) -> generators.Scenario:
    if start not in ("low", "high"):
        raise generators.ScenarioError("start must be low or high")
    phase = 0.0 if start == "low" else cycle_s / 2
    total = n_cycles * cycle_s
    component = generators.triangle("thermal.t_base_k", cycle_s, amp=t_high_c - t_low_c, offset=_c_to_k(t_low_c),
                            absolute=True, slow=compressible, phase_s=phase, t1_s=total, hold_after=True, label="soak",
                            stream="scenario_soak", provenance="read-off", source="LM26-S",
                            note="slide 10 left: 33-108 degC, ~90 cycles of ~20.3 min, ~0.124 degC/s, 30.4 h")
    return generators.Scenario(name="soak", components=(component,), time_compression=time_compression,
        duration_s=total,
                               slow_cycle_s=cycle_s,
                               description=f"soak {t_low_c}-{t_high_c} degC, {n_cycles} x {cycle_s / 60:.1f} min "
                                           f"({(t_high_c - t_low_c) / (cycle_s / 2):.3f} degC/s)",
                               provenance=({"item": "soak", "value": [t_low_c, t_high_c, cycle_s, n_cycles],
                                            "provenance": "read-off", "source": "LM26-S",
                                            "note": "01 section 2.5, D5"},))

returns: generators.Scenario(name='soak', components=(component,), time_compression=time_compression, duration_s=total, slow_cycle_s=cycle_s, description=f'soak {t_low_c}-{t_high_c} degC, {n_cycles} x {cycle_s / 60:.1f} min ({(t_high_c - t_low_c) / (cycle_s / 2):.3f} degC/s)', provenance=({'item': 'soak', 'value': [t_low_c, t_high_c, cycle_s, n_cycles], 'provenance': 'read-off', 'source': 'LM26-S', 'note': '01 section 2.5, D5'},))
